locations.title: Tabby Island
locations.summary: Original home of the Whisken people, twice struck by Cat Cauldron decay and later infiltrated by the Mas'eel Cult.

fields.overview: The original home of the Whisken people. The island first decayed after ancient Whisken created the Cat Cauldron, then decayed again after Tohm awakened it.
fields.history: Ancient Whisken created the Cat Cauldron to improve food and seek the knowledge of what is untasted. It caused the first decay and first exodus, so they buried it beneath the island and erased it from history. Tohm later found it, cooked in it, released a pulse into the earth, and fled with it in the Living Tavern. The Mas'eel sensed the pulse, arrived as false traders, gained village power, and persecuted the Whisken for their Triadic faith.
fields.storyRole: Backstory location, source of Tohm's guilt, Mas'eel infiltration site, and potential future reveal or memory sequence.

relatedEntries.note: Tohm awakened the Cat Cauldron and secretly fled with it.

locations.title: The Everfeast
locations.summary: A heavenly culinary realm where perfect meals are remembered and where the Tablemaker returned after his sacrifice.

fields.overview: A sacred culinary beyond connected to the Tablemaker, holy meals, and the memory of food that heals.
fields.visualIdentity: Endless warm kitchens, impossible banquet tables, golden steam, and meals remembered in perfect form.
fields.history: After the Tablemaker's final meal ended the 300 Year War and cost him his mortal life, his spirit returned to The Everfeast.
fields.gameplayUse: Mythic frame for late-game revelations, Food Essence, and the spiritual meaning of magical cooking.

relatedEntries.note: The Tablemaker returns to The Everfeast.

locations.title: Lillia's Camp
locations.summary: A Faery Realm camp where Lillia uses ambient magic to mass-produce Dark Culinary Arts with Mas'eel support.

fields.overview: Villain-side production site for corrupted meals and late-story enemy logistics.
fields.visualIdentity: Beautiful faery light bent into black kitchen smoke, elegant tents, corrupted banquet stations, and recipe-page worktables.
fields.inhabitants: Princess Lillia, Mas'eel agents, corrupted cooks, and food-magic experiments.
fields.gameplayUse: Potential late-story dungeon, stealth/investigation space, and place to connect Lillia's ambitions to the Mas'eel hunt.

relatedEntries.note: Lillia uses the camp to scale Dark Culinary Arts.
Mur'amar can connect the camp to the Mas'eel network.

locations.title: Whisker Woods
locations.summary: A cozy food-rich forest community of villages, farms, ponds, groves, caves, and taverns that becomes the center of an expanding insect-and-frost corruption.

fields.overview: Main Act I region and Gwen's chosen home after qualifying as a chef.
fields.visualIdentity: Warm earthy colors, bold whimsical trees, cozy tavern culture, flowers, cliffs, ponds, and pockets of dark corruption.
fields.inhabitants: Whisken villagers, Tohm, Kap, Juno, Brambrake, wildlife, slimes, and the intelligent insect colony.
fields.gameplayUse: Hub, gathering region, farms, ponds, bosses, Fire Meal routes, northern caverns, and final hive.
fields.history: Whisken and the Ant Queen once sustained a positive relationship here.

relatedEntries.note: Gwen protects villages and explores this region early.
Tohm rebuilds his life here after Tabby Island.
Mini-boss tied to the corrupted pond.
Planned Act 1 boss tied to cursed bugs.

locations.title: Tohm's Tavern
locations.summary: Gwen's Act I home and hub for the Feast of Full Plates, cooking, quests, Magical Meal development, and character scenes.

fields.overview: A warm living tavern within Whisker Woods where Tohm trains Gwen and serves the community.
fields.history: Connected to Tohm's long travels and hidden culinary research.
fields.gameplayUse: Hub for cooking, quests, conversations, upgrades, and story returns.

locations.title: Kap's Pond
locations.summary: The early Act I rescue location where Gwen saves Kap and defeats a corrupted Prawnhusk.

fields.overview: A fishing pond darkened by corruption and surrounded by aggressive insects.
fields.gameplayUse: Opening rescue, insect combat, Prawnhusk tutorial boss, and later environmental restoration.

locations.title: Northern Whisker Woods
locations.summary: The portion of Whisker Woods consumed by unnatural frost as the Ice Queen's influence spreads.

fields.overview: Frozen roots, altered wildlife, dense nests, and cavern entrances increasingly match Gwen's trance.
fields.gameplayUse: Fire-gated exploration, bosses, colony investigation, and route to the hive.

locations.title: Northern Cavern
locations.summary: The skeletal-root cavern guarded by Thairrott before the deeper insect colony.

fields.overview: Ancient roots, bones, frozen tunnels, and the gateway into organized colony space.
fields.gameplayUse: Thairrott boss and transition from surface exploration into the hive network.

locations.title: Ice Queen's Hive
locations.summary: The organized frozen insect city beneath Whisker Woods and the real location reflected in Gwen's Fire Meal trance.

fields.overview: Egg chambers, food stores, frozen roots, social spaces, defenses, and the Queen's chamber.
fields.history: Once part of a functioning Whisken-insect relationship before Lillia's meal corrupted the Queen.
fields.gameplayUse: Final dungeon, Ice Queen two-phase boss, and first recipe-page recovery.

cultures.title: Whisken Saints
cultures.summary: Whisken Tablekeepers remembered for true Magical Meals given by the Tablemaker.

fields.overview: Holy Whisken teachers and Tablekeepers remembered inside the Tablemaker faith, not a separate religion.
fields.dailyLife: Their stories appear in harvest customs, village proverbs, tavern wall art, and the Festival of Full Plates.
fields.beliefsCustoms: The saints' meals could heal people, lift people into flight, and show the Tablemaker's power through food.
fields.relationships: Tohm's mother tells these stories to him. Gwen eventually fulfills this tradition by cooking the first true Magical Meal of the game.

relatedEntries.note: The Whisken saints thread sits under the Tablemaker faith.
Lady Kiko can embody this tradition in village life.
Gwen is later venerated as a saint in Whisken tradition.

cultures.title: Humans
cultures.summary: Humans are one of the major peoples of the shared Triad civilization, with Ovenhold as their central kingdom and culinary institution.

fields.overview: Important human characters include Gwen, Lillia, the King and Queen, and the unnamed Academy rival.
fields.beliefsGoals: The royal family wants magical access for Lillia despite warnings from faeries and dwarves.
fields.storyRole: Political engine behind the Dragon Knife incident and Lillia's magical transformation.
fields.dailyLife: Ovenhold's human culture gives exceptional prestige to cooking, chefs, hospitality, ritual, and education.
fields.relationships: Humans and faeries share one Triad order after the Tablemaker ended their ancient war.

relatedEntries.note: Princess Lillia is the center of the kingdom's magic crisis.

cultures.title: Whisken People
cultures.summary: A cat-like people tied to Tabby Island, Whisker Woods, tavern culture, food, the Feast of Full Plates, and Tohm Kyatt.

fields.overview: Use the existing canonical spelling and treat Wiscan/Wisken as aliases rather than separate peoples.
fields.dailyLife: Food, hospitality, taverns, fishing, gathering, and communal feasts shape village life.
fields.beliefsCustoms: Most follow the shared Triad faith through Whisken traditions, including the Feast of Full Plates.
fields.exodusHistory: Ancient Whisken buried the Cat Cauldron and erased it from history after the first decay. Modern Whisken fled Tabby Island again after Tohm awakened it and the Mas'eel infiltrated the village.
fields.saintTradition: Whisken Saints are Tablekeeper figures remembered for true Magical Meals. Gwen will later be venerated as one after her life.

relatedEntries.note: Tohm is a Whisken chef with a hidden past.

cultures.title: Faeries
cultures.summary: The people of the Faery Kingdom retain their own culture, hierarchy, military, governance, nobility, and identity within the greater Triad order.

fields.overview: Faeries are not a separate competing religion from Ovenhold's humans.
fields.relationships: The Tablemaker's meal reconciled faeries and humans after the ancient war.

cultures.title: Goblins
cultures.summary: Goblins are established in Act I through Bug, a goblin character who uses lightning magic.

fields.overview: Do not invent an entire goblin civilization beyond existing records.
fields.relationships: Bug is the confirmed Act I example.

cultures.title: Dwarves
cultures.summary: The people of the Dwarven Kingdom are known for powerful magical craftsmanship and originally possessed the Dragon Knife.

fields.overview: The King of Ovenhold wages war after the dwarves refuse to surrender the Dragon Knife.
fields.relationships: The conflict carries major political and moral importance later in the story.

cultures.title: Intelligent Undead
cultures.summary: Cedric proves that intelligent skeletons can speak, negotiate, fear danger, conduct commerce, and change allegiance.

fields.overview: Do not portray every skeleton as mindless or inherently evil.
fields.relationships: Cedric becomes Gwen's recurring Charm-system ally.

factions.title: Mas'eel Cult
factions.summary: A cult that corrupts the Triadic faith into FEAST and hunts the Cat Cauldron and Tohm's magical recipes.

fields.overview: The Mas'eel oppose the Tablemaker's triad of Passion, Taste, and Love by corrupting it into FEAST.
fields.tabbyIslandRole: They sensed the Cat Cauldron pulse, came to Tabby Island pretending to be traders, introduced new foods, gained power in the Whisken village, and persecuted Triadic believers.
fields.currentGoal: After leaving Tabby Island, they search for the Cat Cauldron and Tohm's magical recipes while working with Princess Lillia.

relatedEntries.note: The Mas'eel now work with Lillia.
The Mas'eel are hunting Tohm's recipes and the Cat Cauldron.

factions.title: Mas'eel False Traders
factions.summary: The Mas'eel trading front that entered Tabby Island with new foods and hid a slow takeover behind hospitality.

fields.overview: A disguised Mas'eel operation that looked like trade, novelty, and abundance while spreading control.
fields.leadership: Mur'amar and other Mas'eel agents can use trader identities, food gifts, and gentle public language.
fields.beliefsGoals: Find the Cat Cauldron, locate Tohm's magical recipes, weaken Triadic faith, and replace shared abundance with FEAST.
fields.resourcesPower: Imported foods, suspicious spices, influence inside village ranks, hidden cult marks, and searing corruption.
fields.storyRole: Explains how Tabby Island was corrupted socially and spiritually before the Whisken realized what was happening.

relatedEntries.note: Mur'amar can serve as a recognizable face of this operation.
Tohm's activation of the Cat Cauldron drew the false traders to Tabby Island.

factions.title: Ovenhold
factions.summary: The human civilization and institutional center of the shared Triad order, where cooking, hospitality, and culinary education carry exceptional prestige.

fields.overview: Ovenhold is the central human kingdom and institutional center of the Triad order.
fields.visualIdentity: Stone kitchens, bread ovens, smoke, copper pots, labor-worn hands, hearth banners, and practical warm light.
fields.history: Ovenhold fought the Faery Realm for 300 years until the Tablemaker ended the war with a meal prepared through Passion, Taste, and Love.
fields.gameplayUse: Ancient-history slot, possible memory chapter, religious origin context, and visual contrast to the Faery Realm.
fields.leadership: Led by the King and Queen of Ovenhold; the office remains legitimate even when its holder sins.
fields.beliefsGoals: Food, hospitality, the table, chefs, ritual, and culinary education shape public life.
fields.storyRole: Home of Lillia, the royal family, and the political consequences of the Dragon Knife war.

relatedEntries.note: The Tablemaker's meal ended Ovenhold's war with the Faery Realm.

factions.title: Faery Kingdom
factions.type: Kingdom within the Shared Triad Order
factions.summary: A self-governing faery kingdom that retains its identity, hierarchy, military, and culture while sharing the greater Triad order with Ovenhold.

fields.overview: The Faery Kingdom was once at war with humanity but reconciled through the Tablemaker's final meal.
fields.history: Lillia camps here because the environment lets her draw ambient magic rather than infusing every meal individually.
fields.gameplayUse: Potential late-story region, corrupted meal production source, and faery political space.
fields.leadership: Retains its own nobility, governance, military, hierarchy, and cultural identity.
fields.storyRole: Lel Kai can serve and eventually become General of Ovenhold without abandoning his faery identity.

relatedEntries.note: Lillia uses this realm to empower corrupted food.

factions.title: Dwarven Kingdom
factions.summary: An independent civilization of powerful magical craftsmanship and the original holder of the Dragon Knife.

fields.overview: The dwarves possessed the Dragon Knife and refused the King of Ovenhold's demand for it.
fields.storyRole: The King's war to seize the Knife is one of his major moral failures and part of Lillia's magical origin.

factions.title: Royal House of Ovenhold
factions.summary: The King, Queen, and Princess Lillia, whose family choices connect royal authority to the Dragon Knife and Dark Culinary Arts.

fields.leadership: King and Queen of Ovenhold; Princess Lillia is their daughter.
fields.storyRole: The King's disordered love for Lillia drives the Dragon Knife conflict and creates the conditions for Tohm's unstable dish.

factions.title: Culinary Imperial Academy
factions.summary: The prestigious Academy where Gwen completes her formal education and passes her final qualification examination after apprenticing under Tohm.

fields.overview: Gwen studied here, left for roughly two years of practical apprenticeship under Tohm, then returned for her final examination.
fields.storyRole: The final test requires Gwen to create and present an original dish that proves her culinary identity.
fields.unresolved: Use one Academy record. The relationship between the names Unhold and Ovenhold remains unresolved.

factions.title: Whisken Community of Whisker Woods
factions.summary: The Whisken tavern-and-village community Gwen chooses over the Academy's prestigious Feast celebration.

fields.overview: Includes Tohm, Kap, villagers, farmers, fishers, and the tavern community.
fields.beliefsGoals: Food is shared through hospitality, gratitude, abundance, reconciliation, and communal responsibility.
fields.storyRole: The community gives Gwen a home worth defending throughout Act I.

factions.title: Ant Colony
factions.summary: An organized society beneath Whisker Woods that once cooperated with the Whisken under the Ant Queen before corruption transformed it into a hostile frozen army.

fields.overview: The colony contains hierarchy, gathering, food logistics, nests, chambers, workers, and a ruling Queen.
fields.storyRole: Lillia's corrupted meal changes the Queen and spreads through the colony, creating the Act I crisis.

timeline.title: Ancient Cat Cauldron Disaster
timeline.summary: Ancient Whisken create the Cat Cauldron, trigger Tabby Island decay, flee, bury it, and erase it from history.

fields.event: Ancient Whisken seek better food and knowledge of what is untasted; the Cat Cauldron's power damages Tabby Island.
fields.causes: Good hunger for food knowledge mixed with unsafe magical invention.
fields.consequences: First exodus, Cat Cauldron buried beneath the island, records removed, and the event eventually forgotten.
fields.involved: Ancient Whisken, Tabby Island, Cat Cauldron, Tablemaker faith.

relatedEntries.note: Sentient artifact tied to this ancient disaster.

timeline.title: Tohm Seeks a Flavor Unlike Anything Anyone Had Ever Tasted
timeline.summary: Tohm's life is driven by the need to find a flavor unlike anything anyone had ever tasted.

fields.event: After making everything there was to make and tasting everything there was to taste, Tohm reflects on the Tablemaker stories his mother told him.
fields.causes: Sweet taste buds, total culinary boredom, and stories of saints making Magical Meals.
fields.consequences: Tohm begins years of travel, secret study, and obsession that lead him to the Living Tavern and Cat Cauldron.
fields.involved: Tohm Kyatt, Whisken Saints, Tablemaker stories.

relatedEntries.note: This is Tohm's core drive.

timeline.title: Tohm Discovers the Living Tavern
timeline.summary: Tohm discovers the Living Tavern during his long search for Magical Meal knowledge.

fields.event: During years of grinding, travel, disappearance, and secret culinary work, Tohm discovers the Living Tavern.
fields.causes: His search for a way to make Magical Meals and taste the impossible flavor.
fields.consequences: The Living Tavern becomes Tohm's home, workshop, and eventual escape route with the Cat Cauldron.
fields.involved: Tohm Kyatt, Living Tavern, Cat Cauldron.

relatedEntries.note: The Living Tavern becomes Tohm's mobile workshop.

timeline.title: Tohm Awakens the Cat Cauldron
timeline.summary: Tohm discovers the forgotten Cat Cauldron, cooks in it, releases a pulse into the earth, and secretly flees with it.

fields.event: Tohm cooks a meal in the Cat Cauldron and activates it.
fields.causes: Tohm's obsession with magical food, the Tablemaker stories, and the knowledge of what is untasted.
fields.consequences: Tabby Island begins dying again, the Mas'eel sense the cauldron, and Tohm flees with it in the Living Tavern.
fields.involved: Tohm Kyatt, Cat Cauldron, Tabby Island, Mas'eel Cult.

relatedEntries.note: Tohm is the one who awakens the cauldron.

timeline.title: Cat Cauldron Cannot Teach Magical Meals
timeline.summary: The Cat Cauldron knows culinary secrets from around the world, but cannot answer how to make a true Magical Meal.

fields.event: Tohm asks the Cat Cauldron's knowledge to solve true Magical Meals and finds that even it does not know.
fields.causes: The Cat Cauldron holds chef knowledge and culinary abilities, not the Tablemaker's gift.
fields.consequences: Tohm keeps experimenting from his own expertise and unknowingly moves toward a Dark Magical Meal.
fields.involved: Tohm Kyatt, Cat Cauldron, Magical Meals.

relatedEntries.note: Tohm keeps going after the cauldron fails to answer him.

timeline.title: Tohm Creates a Dark Magical Meal
timeline.summary: Tohm believes he has created a Magical Meal, but it is actually a Dark Magical Meal.

fields.event: After long experimentation, Tohm creates what he thinks is a Magical Meal.
fields.causes: Tohm seeks magic through expertise and the Cat Cauldron rather than through the Tablemaker.
fields.consequences: The meal's power comes from a dark source, setting up Lillia's transformation.
fields.involved: Tohm Kyatt, Cat Cauldron, Dark Culinary Arts, Princess Lillia.

relatedEntries.note: Tohm is responsible but does not understand what he made.

timeline.title: Lillia Consumes the Dark Magical Meal
timeline.summary: Princess Lillia sneaks around, eats Tohm's Dark Magical Meal, and receives dark magic.

fields.event: Lillia eats the meal Tohm thinks is his first Magical Meal.
fields.causes: Lillia is sneaking around on the night of Tohm's apparent success.
fields.consequences: Lillia gains dark magic, later tears pages from Tohm's recipe book, and begins the Dark Culinary Arts threat.
fields.involved: Princess Lillia, Tohm Kyatt, Tohm's Recipe Book.

relatedEntries.note: This is the secret origin of Lillia's dark magic.

timeline.title: Mas'eel Infiltrate Tabby Island
timeline.summary: Mas'eel cultists arrive as false traders, introduce new foods, gain power, and persecute the Whisken faith.

fields.event: The Mas'eel trading front enters Tabby Island after sensing the Cat Cauldron pulse.
fields.causes: They know the Cat Cauldron was on Tabby Island and want Tohm's recipes.
fields.consequences: Whisken village authority is corrupted, Triadic believers are persecuted, and the second exodus begins.
fields.involved: Mas'eel Cult, Whisken People, Mur'amar, False Trader Spice, Tabby Island.

relatedEntries.note: Mur'amar can be connected to this infiltration thread.

timeline.title: Lel Kai's Rescue Fleet
timeline.summary: Lel Kai sends boats at Tohm's request, but corruption scatters many of them before the known survivors reach Whisker Woods.

fields.event: Rescue boats leave for Tabby Island during the second exodus.
fields.causes: Tohm hears what is happening and gets Lel Kai, who is becoming general of the faery army, to help.
fields.consequences: Known survivors settle in Whisker Woods and Whisken Village; scattered boats and missing survivors remain open story hooks.
fields.involved: Tohm Kyatt, Lel Kai, Whisken People, Tabby Island, Whisker Woods.

relatedEntries.note: Tohm initiates the rescue after hiding his own earlier role.

timeline.title: Tohm Writes the Fire Meal
timeline.summary: Tohm writes the Fire Meal after losing his dark magical recipes, but refuses to cook it himself.

fields.event: Tohm begins a new recipe after Lillia tears out pages from his recipe book.
fields.causes: Fear, shame, and the need to keep seeking a Magical Meal without repeating the disaster himself.
fields.consequences: Tohm mentors Gwen and eventually asks her to cook the Fire Meal during the Feast of Full Plates.
fields.involved: Tohm Kyatt, Gwen, Fire Meal, Tohm's Recipe Book.

relatedEntries.note: Tohm writes the recipe but will not cook it himself.

timeline.title: Feast of Full Plates Night
timeline.summary: Gwen cooks Tohm's Fire Meal during the holy Feast of Full Plates while the village watches.

fields.event: Gwen gathers ingredients and cooks the Fire Meal during the Feast of Full Plates.
fields.causes: Tohm has written the Fire Meal for years and asks Gwen to be the one to try it.
fields.consequences: The meal appears to fail publicly, Tohm hides heartbreak, and Gwen serves the feast.
fields.involved: Gwen, Tohm Kyatt, Lel Kai, Whisken villagers, Fire Meal.

relatedEntries.note: Gwen cooks during the opening feast.

timeline.title: Gwen Cooks the First True Magical Meal
timeline.summary: Gwen's Fire Meal becomes the first true Magical Meal of the game because she cooks in the Tablemaker's name.

fields.event: Gwen's cooking prayer directs the Fire Meal toward the Tablemaker.
fields.causes: Gwen is a devoted Tablekeeper who has cooked in the Tablemaker's name since childhood.
fields.consequences: The Fire Meal becomes true rather than dark, though Tohm, Gwen, and Lel Kai do not know why.
fields.involved: Gwen, The Tablemaker, Tohm Kyatt, Fire Meal.

relatedEntries.note: Gwen's devotion is the hidden difference.

timeline.title: Gwen Wakes in the Snowstorm
timeline.summary: After the feast, Gwen eats the Fire Meal, enters a trance, and wakes in a snowstorm.

fields.event: Gwen takes a bite of the Fire Meal after the villagers leave.
fields.causes: The meal's true Magical Meal power activates after Gwen eats it.
fields.consequences: Gwen enters a trance and wakes in a snowstorm. Stop this arc there for now.
fields.involved: Gwen, Tohm Kyatt, Lel Kai, Fire Meal.

relatedEntries.note: This is Gwen's first Magical Meal aftermath.

magicSystems.title: Dark Culinary Arts
magicSystems.summary: A dangerous practice born from Tohm's first failed Magical Meal attempt and later weaponized by Lillia.

fields.overview: Corrupted culinary magic that imitates true Magical Meals through a dark source rather than the Tablemaker.
fields.rules: Tohm's first apparent Magical Meal was actually a Dark Magical Meal because he sought magic apart from the Tablemaker. Lillia ate it, received dark magic, and later learned to corrupt food at scale. Consumers may gain powers or become corrupted. Faery ambient magic helps mass-produce it.
fields.visualEffects: Dark glowing ingredients, corrupted meal auras, unstable magic, and theatrical food-based powers.
fields.storyFunction: Explains corrupted bosses, recipe-powered enemies, and magical food as both power and danger.

relatedEntries.note: Lillia spreads corrupted meals through this magic.

magicSystems.title: Food Essence
magicSystems.summary: The spiritual and magical force released into the world by the Tablemaker after the meal that ended the 300 Year War.

fields.overview: Food Essence is the sacred foundation that lets meals carry healing, memory, culture, magic, danger, and true Magical Meal power.
fields.rules: Healthy Food Essence is aligned with Passion, Taste, and Love. True Magical Meals are Tablemaker-given expressions of it. Dark Culinary Arts, Dark Magical Meals, and Mas'eel FEAST doctrine distort it toward control, hunger, and corruption.
fields.visualEffects: Warm steam, golden motes, meal-memory glows, and three-dot Triadic symbolism when expressed cleanly.
fields.gameplayFunction: Frames why cooking can heal, empower, reveal, corrupt, and solve story problems.
fields.storyFunction: Connects the Tablemaker, Tohm's obsession, Gwen's Fire Meal, Lillia's corrupted meals, and the Mas'eel distortion.

relatedEntries.note: The Tablemaker released Food Essence into the world.
Tohm's obsession grows around sacred food and ultimate taste.
Gwen's Fire Meal works through the Tablemaker's power.

magicSystems.title: Magical Meals
magicSystems.summary: True Tablemaker-given meals that can heal, empower, reveal, or grant miraculous abilities.

fields.overview: True Magical Meals are not simply recipes. They are meals empowered by the Tablemaker through faithful cooking.
fields.rules: Whisken Saints made true Magical Meals through the Tablemaker. Tohm's technical search produces a Dark Magical Meal, while Gwen's Fire Meal becomes true because she cooks in the Tablemaker's name.
fields.visualEffects: Warm sacred steam, clean fire, three-dot Triadic glows, meal memories, and miracle effects that feel different from Lillia's dark magic.
fields.storyFunction: Creates the central twist between Tohm's failed dark meal and Gwen's true Fire Meal.

relatedEntries.note: Gwen cooks the first true Magical Meal of the game.
Tohm spends his life trying to discover how to make one.
True Magical Meals come from the Tablemaker.

foodAndRecipes.title: Festival of Full Plates
foodAndRecipes.summary: A holy Whisken feast celebrating balance, gratitude, remembrance, and the promise that no plate should go empty.

fields.overview: A Whisken holy feast and village tradition tied to shared abundance under the Tablemaker faith. In village speech it is also called the Feast of Full Plates.
fields.culinaryUse: Built around Hearth Stew, Healthy Ale, roots, herbs, gathered produce, and everyone being fed.
fields.gameplayUse: Opening feast event, reputation moment, recipe set, cultural tutorial, and setup for Gwen cooking the Fire Meal.
fields.magicalEffect: Can quietly express healthy Food Essence through Passion, Taste, and Love without becoming a combat spell.
fields.openingNight: Whisken villagers and Lel Kai attend while Gwen cooks Tohm's Fire Meal. The public miracle appears to fail before the meal works later.

relatedEntries.note: Lady Kiko can guide or protect this tradition.
Gwen cooks the Fire Meal on this night.
Lel Kai attends the feast and witnesses Gwen's trance.

foodAndRecipes.title: Healthy Ale
foodAndRecipes.summary: Oswin's famous Whisken ale; villagers rely on it even though the name is mostly optimistic.

fields.overview: A village drink and recipe slot in The Pantry.
fields.culinaryUse: Whisken Root Ferment, Moonlit Dew, and Specialty Herbs make it feel medicinal, odd, and tavern-ready.
fields.gameplayUse: Possible stamina, warmth, light recovery, or comedic side-effect drink.
fields.magicalEffect: Should stay lightly magical or alchemical unless later upgraded.

relatedEntries.note: Oswin invented Healthy Ale.

foodAndRecipes.title: Whisken Hearth Stew
foodAndRecipes.summary: A hearty Whisken stew built from roots, broth, herbs, and safe village ingredients.

fields.overview: Practical comfort recipe for the Pantry and Whisken Village food culture.
fields.culinaryUse: Potato, Turnip, Boga, Specialty Herbs, and Cat Cauldron Broth Base.
fields.gameplayUse: Starter recovery meal, comfort meal, village favor, or cooking tutorial recipe.
fields.magicalEffect: A clean everyday Food Essence expression: feeding people before chasing power.

relatedEntries.note: Momon anchors the farming side of this meal.
Mona can provide produce or orchard timing.

foodAndRecipes.title: False Trader Spice
foodAndRecipes.summary: A suspicious spice blend introduced by Mas'eel false traders during their slow infiltration of Tabby Island.

fields.overview: Ingredient and clue that food culture was used as cover for the Mas'eel takeover.
fields.culinaryUse: Looks like an exciting imported spice, but belongs in corrupted recipes and investigation scenes.
fields.gameplayUse: Quest evidence, dangerous recipe component, debuff ingredient, or clue leading to Mur'amar.
fields.magicalEffect: Can carry searing corruption or distort healthy Food Essence toward FEAST.

relatedEntries.note: Mur'amar may use gentle language around this kind of imported food.

foodAndRecipes.title: Cat Cauldron Broth Base
foodAndRecipes.summary: A flexible broth base made in the Cat Cauldron for stews, magical meals, and comfort dishes.

fields.overview: Everyday Pantry slot for the Cat Cauldron's normal cooking use.
fields.culinaryUse: Any safe meat or creature drop, produce, and Specialty Herbs simmered into a flexible base.
fields.gameplayUse: Meal component for Hearth Stew, magical meals, restorative recipes, and cooking tutorials.
fields.magicalEffect: Separates normal broth work from the catastrophic act of awakening the ancient cauldron.

relatedEntries.note: The sentient cauldron is the station for this recipe.

foodAndRecipes.title: Gwen's Graduation Dish
foodAndRecipes.summary: The original dish Gwen creates for her final Academy examination and later recreates for Tohm during the Feast of Full Plates.

fields.overview: Represents Gwen's own culinary identity after Academy study and Tohm's apprenticeship.
fields.culinaryUse: Final name and exact recipe remain intentionally unresolved.
fields.storyFunction: Proves Gwen is a qualified chef and gives her homecoming feast personal meaning.

foodAndRecipes.title: Fire Meal
foodAndRecipes.summary: Gwen's first major Magical Meal grants fire-based combat power and pulls her into a trance connected to Lillia, the Ant Queen, and the real hive beneath Whisker Woods.

fields.overview: Prepared through Tohm's recipe and Gwen's cooking; exact final ingredient list remains editable.
fields.culinaryUse: Tohm asks Gwen to gather the ingredients before the big night. Ingredient details can be expanded in The Pantry as the recipe design develops.
fields.gameplayUse: Flaming sword, burn damage, explosive heat, cold resistance, projectiles, or a fire ultimate according to final combat design.
fields.magicalEffect: Triggers Gwen's first trance and becomes the main counter to the Ice Queen.
fields.storyFunction: Connects cooking, combat progression, memory, and the Act I mystery.

relatedEntries.note: Gwen cooks the Fire Meal and enters the snowstorm trance.
Tohm writes it but fears cooking it himself.
The Tablemaker gives the true Magical Meal power.

foodAndRecipes.title: Blizzard Meal
foodAndRecipes.summary: The likely ice-associated meal Lillia gives the trusting Ant Queen, transforming her into the Ice Queen; exact final name remains reviewable.

fields.overview: A torn-page recipe connected to the Ice Queen's corruption and recovered after the Act I boss.
fields.magicalEffect: Transforms the Ant Queen, spreads frost through the colony, and creates magical winter.
fields.unresolved: Use Blizzard Meal unless a newer confirmed Ice Meal name supersedes it.

creatureLinks.title: Cauldron Echo Slime
creatureLinks.summary: A rare slime formed near places touched by Cat Cauldron pulses and old recipe memory.

fields.loreNote: This creature gives the Cat Cauldron disaster a visible ecosystem consequence.
fields.ecosystem: Appears near buried kitchens, ruins, broth residue, and pulse-touched ground.
fields.gameplayStoryLinks: Drops Cauldron echo gel for truth-reveal tonics and late-game investigation meals.

relatedEntries.note: Bestiary slot seeded from Cat Cauldron lore.

creatureLinks.title: Seared Scarab
creatureLinks.summary: An insect tied to Mas'eel searing, false trader stores, and corrupted Tabby Island roots.

fields.loreNote: A small enemy that makes the Mas'eel's slow corruption visible in the environment.
fields.ecosystem: Clusters around corrupted roots, old food stores, and false trader caches.
fields.gameplayStoryLinks: Drops Seared shell chips and traces of False Trader Spice.

relatedEntries.note: Bestiary slot seeded for Mas'eel corruption.

creatureLinks.title: False Feast Fly
creatureLinks.summary: A deceptive swarm drawn to food that looks abundant but has been spiritually spoiled.

fields.loreNote: A creature-symbol for the Mas'eel version of abundance: hunger wearing a beautiful mask.
fields.ecosystem: Appears near corrupted feasts, rotten ceremonial leftovers, and Dark Culinary Arts experiments.
fields.gameplayStoryLinks: Drops False feast wings for deception tonics and corruption-diagnosis recipes.

relatedEntries.note: Bestiary slot seeded for FEAST symbolism.

characterLinks.summary: A reserved Whisken orchardist who connects village produce, family, and longing for the wider world.

fields.worldRole: Whisken Village orchardist and possible produce source.
fields.relationships: Daughter of Momon; connected to Gwen's gathering work and village routines.
fields.automaticLinks: Whisken Village, Whisken People, Festival of Full Plates, Moonlit Dew, Whisken Hearth Stew.

relatedEntries.note: Main database character entry.

characterLinks.title: Momon
characterLinks.summary: A Whisken farmer who anchors village food production and passes agricultural knowledge to Mona.

fields.relationships: Father of Mona; village peer to Kap, Oswin, and Lady Kiko.
fields.automaticLinks: Whisken Village, Festival of Full Plates, Whisken Hearth Stew, Potato, Turnip, Boga.

relatedEntries.note: Main database character entry.

characterLinks.title: Lady Kiko
characterLinks.summary: A protective Whisken guide who expresses unity, faith, and community care.

fields.worldRole: Protector, mediator, or cultural guide for Whisken Village.
fields.relationships: Linked to village families, Gwen's learning of Whisken customs, and the Festival of Full Plates.
fields.automaticLinks: Whisken People, Whisken Saints, Whisken Village, Festival of Full Plates.

relatedEntries.note: Main database character entry.

characterLinks.summary: A Mas'eel-linked stranger who presents his faith gently while searching for the Cat Cauldron and recipes.

fields.worldRole: Cult agent or linked figure moving through Whisken spaces under a peaceful mask.
fields.relationships: Speaks with Gwen, moves among villagers as if he belongs, and connects to Princess Lillia's broader villain network.

characterLinks.title: The Tablemaker
characterLinks.summary: The divine figure also called the Master Chef, source of the Tablemaker faith, Food Essence, and true Magical Meals.

fields.relationships: Inspires Tohm's childhood stories, empowers true Magical Meals, and opposes the Mas'eel distortion of FEAST.

myths.title: Triad Faith
myths.summary: The shared religious, philosophical, cultural, and gameplay order centered on Love, Taste, and Passion.

fields.overview: Love, Taste, and Passion are spiritual principles, cultural values, and gameplay ideas. The Triad sets the principles by which authority and life should be judged.
fields.fullStory: The Master Chef is another name for the Tablemaker, not a separate being. The faith's central triad is Passion, Taste, and Love. Devoted followers are called Tablekeepers.
fields.meaning: A sinful ruler does not make the Triad false. Legitimate earthly authority can remain legitimate while an individual leader acts wrongly.
fields.magicalMeals: True Magical Meals are Tablemaker-given. Tohm's first apparent success is dark because he seeks power apart from the Tablemaker, while Gwen's Fire Meal works because she cooks in his name.
fields.storyRole: The Tablemaker's sacrificial meal ended the ancient human-faery war and founded their shared order.

relatedEntries.note: Stories of the Tablemaker seed Tohm's obsession with sacred meals and untasted food.
Gwen is a devoted Tablekeeper whose cooking prayer matters.

items.title: Cat Cauldron
items.summary: An ancient Whisken cauldron created to improve food and reveal what is untasted, later awakened by Tohm and hunted by the Mas'eel.

fields.overview: An ancient Whisken artifact that caused Tabby Island to decay once in antiquity and again after Tohm activated it.
fields.powersUses: Created to improve food and reach the knowledge of what is untasted. It holds secrets of chefs and culinary abilities around the world, but it cannot teach Tohm how to make a true Magical Meal. When activated, it can send a pulse into the earth strong enough to decay land and draw the Mas'eel's attention.
fields.history: The ancient Whisken buried it beneath Tabby Island and erased it from history. Tohm later discovered it, cooked in it, awakened it, and fled with it in the Living Tavern.

relatedEntries.note: Tohm awakened the cauldron and secretly took it.

items.title: Academy Qualification
items.summary: Proof that Gwen passed the Culinary Imperial Academy's final examination and is officially qualified as a chef.

fields.overview: Earned immediately before Gwen returns to Whisker Woods.
fields.history: Tohm examines it with rare visible pride during the Feast of Full Plates.

items.title: Gwen's Sword
items.summary: Gwen's primary combat weapon and the focus through which she first channels the Fire Meal.

fields.powersUses: Baseline sword combat; can become flame-wreathed while Fire Meal power is active.

items.title: Gwen's Basket
items.summary: Gwen's practical gathering identity item, used to carry ingredients gathered across Whisker Woods.

fields.powersUses: Supports gathering, ingredient collection, and Gwen's visual identity.

items.title: Tohm's Recipe Book
items.summary: Tohm's book of dangerous culinary knowledge, from which Lillia tears pages that later spread the Dark Culinary Arts.

fields.history: Tohm keeps the main book during his struggle with Lillia, but she escapes with multiple torn pages.
fields.powersUses: Source of powerful Magical Meal knowledge and the long-term recovery quest.

items.title: Recipe Pages
items.summary: Pages torn from Tohm's Recipe Book that carry dangerous culinary magic, empower corrupted bosses, and become Gwen's long-term recovery objective.

fields.definition: Torn pages from Tohm's magical recipe book.
fields.longExplanation: Lillia tears out several pages after eating Tohm's Dark Magical Meal and after Tohm snatches the recipe book back. Gwen retrieves recipe pages from bosses to unlock powers, restore lost culinary knowledge, and eventually expose the difference between true Magical Meals and Dark Magical Meals.
fields.powersUses: Recovered from bosses to restore knowledge, unlock meals, and reveal the truth behind Dark Culinary Arts.
fields.history: Lillia tore them from Tohm's book after consuming his unstable dark meal.

relatedEntries.note: Gwen recovers recipe pages through the main quest.
The pages came from Tohm's recipe book.
Lillia tore the pages out.

items.title: Dragon Knife
items.summary: A powerful dwarven artifact seized after the King of Ovenhold wages war in his attempt to grant Lillia magic.

fields.history: The Dwarven Kingdom refuses to surrender it; Ovenhold's King goes to war and takes it.
fields.powersUses: Later becomes part of Tohm's dangerous creation of the meal that gives Lillia magic.

items.title: Charms
items.summary: Passive or modifying equipment managed through Cedric's recurring merchant and upgrade role.

fields.powersUses: Sell, equip, improve, modify, or upgrade gameplay bonuses.
fields.history: Cedric turns his survival after Gwen defeats him into an ongoing business relationship.

quests.title: Lel Kai's Rescue Fleet
quests.summary: Tohm asks Lel Kai to send boats to rescue the Whisken from Tabby Island during the second exodus.

fields.overview: Rescue-fleet event explaining how the known Whisken survivors reached Whisker Woods.
fields.objectives: Gather boats, cross corrupted waters, save as many Whisken as possible, and survive scattered routes.
fields.majorBeats: Tohm hears what is happening, gets Lel Kai's help, boats are sent, corruption scatters many, known survivors reach Whisker Woods.
fields.rewardsConsequences: The current Whisken Village exists, but missing boats and survivor trauma remain story hooks.

relatedEntries.note: Tohm sets the rescue in motion.
Kap represents the current survivor village generation.

quests.title: Investigate the False Traders
quests.summary: A quest thread for uncovering how Mas'eel trade, spices, and gentle language corrupted Tabby Island.

fields.overview: Investigation line connecting suspicious foods, cult signs, creature evidence, and Mur'amar's public mask.
fields.objectives: Inspect trader stores, identify False Trader Spice, fight Seared Scarabs or False Feast Flies, question Mur'amar, and connect clues to the Cat Cauldron pulse.
fields.majorBeats: The player realizes that food was not just flavor here. It was the method of takeover.
fields.rewardsConsequences: Unlocks Mas'eel truth, Dark Culinary Arts context, and Tabby Island history.

relatedEntries.note: Mur'amar is a key face for this investigation.

quests.title: Feast of Full Plates Opening Night
quests.summary: Gwen gathers ingredients, cooks the Fire Meal at the holy feast, serves the village, and wakes in a snowstorm.

fields.overview: Opening arc where Tohm's years of Fire Meal work meet Gwen's Tablekeeper devotion.
fields.objectives: Gather Fire Meal ingredients, return before the Feast of Full Plates, cook the meal, help serve the feast, then eat the meal after the villagers leave.
fields.majorBeats: The meal appears to fail in front of everyone. Tohm hides heartbreak. Gwen later eats a bite, enters a trance, and wakes in a snowstorm.
fields.rewardsConsequences: Starts the true Magical Meal arc and hides the central twist that Gwen's Tablemaker prayer is why the meal works.

relatedEntries.note: Gwen performs the cooking that starts the game arc.
Tohm writes the Fire Meal but does not cook it himself.
Lel Kai attends and witnesses the aftermath.

quests.title: The Final Test
quests.summary: Gwen earns the title of chef before choosing where she belongs.

fields.overview: Gwen earns the title of chef before choosing where she belongs.
fields.storyBeats:
After roughly two years of practical apprenticeship under the legendary Whisken chef Tohm Kyatt, Gwen returns to the Culinary Imperial Academy of Unhold for the final stage of her education. The apprenticeship made her capable, but it did not make her officially qualified. To graduate, she must conceptualize, prepare, cook, and present a dish of her own design before the Academy judges.

The test asks more than whether she can follow instructions. Gwen must show judgment, technique, and a culinary identity shaped by both formal Academy discipline and Tohm's improvisational teaching. The judges taste her dish and pass her. Gwen leaves the examination as a newly qualified chef, carrying proof that the difficult years away from home meant something. The final name and recipe of her graduation dish remain intentionally unresolved.
fields.objectives: Gwen enters Act I as a qualified chef rather than a beginner, and her graduation dish becomes a symbol of her own culinary voice.
fields.connectedWorldbuilding: Gwen, Tohm Kyatt, Culinary Imperial Academy, Gwen's Graduation Dish, Academy Qualification
fields.chronology: Act I — The Queen Beneath the Frost · Chapter 1 of 34

quests.title: Gwen Chooses Home
quests.summary: The Feast of Full Plates gives Gwen a choice between prestige and community.

fields.overview: The Feast of Full Plates gives Gwen a choice between prestige and community.
fields.storyBeats:
Gwen's qualification falls on the Feast of Full Plates, when the Academy and Ovenhold hold an enormous prestigious celebration. She could remain among celebrated chefs and enjoy the recognition she has earned. Instead, she leaves for Whisker Woods.

Gwen wants to spend the feast with Tohm, Juno, Kap, and the Whisken community that became her second home. The decision quietly defines her priorities. Prestige matters less than the people who fed her, trained her, argued with her, and gave her a place at their table. Whisker Woods is not merely where Tohm's tavern happens to stand. It is the community Gwen chooses.
fields.objectives: Her homecoming and the sacred feast become one celebration, establishing community as Gwen's central motivation.
fields.connectedWorldbuilding: Gwen, Feast of Full Plates, Whisker Woods, Tohm Kyatt, Juno, Kap
fields.chronology: Act I — The Queen Beneath the Frost · Chapter 2 of 34

quests.title: Something Is Wrong with Whisker Woods
quests.summary: A familiar road shows the first signs of an organized corruption.

fields.overview: A familiar road shows the first signs of an organized corruption.
fields.storyBeats:
The path home should be familiar, but Whisker Woods feels wrong almost immediately. Insects appear in unusual numbers. Beetles and Dappleflies behave with unnatural aggression, egg clusters cling to places where they should not exist, and frightened wildlife has been pushed out of its normal territory.

The signs do not yet form a complete answer, but they are too consistent to dismiss as a bad season. Something is disturbing the forest's food chain and directing creatures that should be scattered. When Gwen hears Kap screaming from the direction of his pond, the unease becomes an immediate crisis.
fields.objectives: Gwen's homecoming becomes an investigation before she even reaches the feast.
fields.connectedWorldbuilding: Gwen, Whisker Woods, Dappleflies, Crayhusks, Kap's Pond
fields.chronology: Act I — The Queen Beneath the Frost · Chapter 3 of 34

quests.title: Kap's Corrupted Pond
quests.summary: Gwen's first day as a chef becomes her first rescue.

fields.overview: Gwen's first day as a chef becomes her first rescue.
fields.storyBeats:
Gwen reaches Kap's Pond and finds its water darkened by corruption, its vegetation dying, and its banks crowded with hostile insects. Kap is trapped near damaged fishing gear while bugs close around him. Gwen fights through the swarm to reach him, only for the disturbed water to erupt beneath them.

A giant corrupted Prawnhusk rises from the pond. The armored creature turns the rescue into Gwen's first major combat test after returning home. She reads its heavy claw attacks, survives its territorial charges, and defeats it long enough to get Kap to safety. The victory proves Gwen can protect this community, but the residue around the creature makes one fact unavoidable: the forest is not suffering from an ordinary infestation.
fields.objectives: Kap is saved, while the Prawnhusk provides the first undeniable evidence that the forest itself is being changed.
fields.connectedWorldbuilding: Gwen, Kap, Kap's Pond, Prawnhusk, Whisker Woods
fields.chronology: Act I — The Queen Beneath the Frost · Chapter 4 of 34

quests.title: Feast of Full Plates
quests.summary: A sacred community feast becomes Gwen's homecoming and graduation celebration.

fields.overview: A sacred community feast becomes Gwen's homecoming and graduation celebration.
fields.storyBeats:
Gwen reaches the village after nightfall and finds Tohm's tavern overflowing with lantern light, music, food, and Whisken families. The Feast of Full Plates celebrates food shared rather than hoarded: hospitality, gratitude, abundance, reconciliation, and the promise that no one at the table should remain hungry. This year it also celebrates Gwen's return as a qualified chef.

Tohm's first response is a dry, 'You're late.' Kap's account of the pond and Prawnhusk finally earns Gwen his full attention. Tohm examines her Academy qualification with rare visible pride, then immediately puts her to work. Because he missed the examination, he asks Gwen to recreate the dish that earned her qualification. As they cook side by side, villagers trade rumors about lost produce, insect nests, dangerous roads, and frost appearing in the wrong season. Gwen notices that Tohm reacts to the mention of the cold before hiding it.
fields.objectives: Gwen is welcomed home, her identity as a chef is affirmed, and Tohm's first suspicious reaction plants doubt beneath the warmth.
fields.connectedWorldbuilding: Gwen, Tohm Kyatt, Feast of Full Plates, Tohm's Tavern, Gwen's Graduation Dish, Whisken People
fields.chronology: Act I — The Queen Beneath the Frost · Chapter 5 of 34

quests.title: Juno's Friendly Fight
quests.summary: A familiar sparring partner tests whether Gwen's long training dulled her instincts.

fields.overview: A familiar sparring partner tests whether Gwen's long training dulled her instincts.
fields.storyBeats:
Juno challenges Gwen to a friendly spar rather than a hostile duel. Their teasing makes it clear that this is a familiar language between friends: competitive, affectionate, and sharp enough that neither can be careless.

Juno blocks, dodges, punishes reckless attacks, and forces Gwen to think about spacing and timing. The encounter teaches the player combat fundamentals without pretending Gwen has never held a sword. She is already a capable fighter. Later, when the Fire Meal gives Gwen supernatural power, Juno serves the same purpose again by reminding her that flames cannot replace discipline.
fields.objectives: The player learns Gwen's baseline combat before Magical Meals alter it.
fields.connectedWorldbuilding: Gwen, Juno, Whisker Woods, Fire Meal
fields.chronology: Act I — The Queen Beneath the Frost · Chapter 6 of 34

quests.title: Life as a Chef in Whisker Woods
quests.summary: The game's everyday loop grows naturally from Gwen's place in the tavern.

fields.overview: The game's everyday loop grows naturally from Gwen's place in the tavern.
fields.storyBeats:
For a time, Gwen settles into the work she returned to do. Tohm needs ingredients, so she explores, gathers, hunts, fights, and brings food home to cook. Turnips, herbs, Sunchee, Purfox, fruit, meat, and slime-derived ingredients make the forest feel like a living pantry rather than a corridor between battles.

The routine introduces ordinary meals, healing ales and tonics, and smaller snacks that provide temporary strength, stamina, recovery, resistance, or mobility before Gwen ever masters a Magical Meal. Slimes belong to the food ecosystem as sources of flavor and substitution, with different gels supporting recipes and consumables. Gwen's complicated history with ale remains part of her character, but it does not reduce every tavern interaction to that struggle. The cozy loop gives the spreading corruption something meaningful to threaten.
fields.objectives: The player learns the food-and-adventure loop and develops a practical reason to care about the forest's health.
fields.connectedWorldbuilding: Gwen, Tohm Kyatt, Whisker Woods, Ales and Tonics, Snacks, Slime Substitutions
fields.chronology: Act I — The Queen Beneath the Frost · Chapter 7 of 34

quests.title: The Magical Boar
quests.summary: A hunt proves that the corruption is moving through what creatures consume.

fields.overview: A hunt proves that the corruption is moving through what creatures consume.
fields.storyBeats:
A search for stronger ingredients leads Gwen to a boar that has become unnaturally powerful. The animal charges hard enough to break trees and forces Gwen to rely on timing, positioning, and patience rather than simple aggression.

When it falls, Gwen finds magical residue associated with what the boar consumed. The encounter advances the culinary progression — better and stranger ingredients can create stronger food — while revealing its dark mirror. The forest's food chain is being poisoned or manipulated, and creatures are changing because of what enters their bodies.
fields.objectives: Gwen gains a rare ingredient and the investigation shifts toward food as the mechanism of corruption.
fields.connectedWorldbuilding: Gwen, Magical Boar, Whisker Woods, Magical Meals, Corruption Through Consumption
fields.chronology: Act I — The Queen Beneath the Frost · Chapter 8 of 34

quests.title: The Academy Rival
quests.summary: A Cook Battle measures what Tohm's apprenticeship added to Gwen's formal training.

fields.overview: A Cook Battle measures what Tohm's apprenticeship added to Gwen's formal training.
fields.storyBeats:
A former Academy classmate challenges Gwen to a Cook Battle. The rival is competitive but not hateful: she understands Gwen's stubbornness, recognizes the influence of Tohm's teaching, and favors precision and formal technique over wilderness improvisation.

The competition tests Taste, Technique, and Presentation through ingredient choice, heat, preparation, seasoning, timing, recovery, and risk. The rival initially dismisses one of Gwen's slime-derived substitutions as crude. Gwen makes it work by combining Academy discipline with the adaptability she learned in Whisker Woods. The result proves that her years under Tohm did not interrupt her education; they completed a missing part of it. The rival or nearby caravan also brings news of unnatural frost along the northern road. Her canonical name remains Academy Rival — Name TBD; Ressa Vale is only a retired working-name note.
fields.objectives: Gwen proves her hybrid cooking style and receives another clue pointing north.
fields.connectedWorldbuilding: Gwen, Academy Rival — Name TBD, Culinary Imperial Academy, Cook Battle, Slime Substitutions
fields.chronology: Act I — The Queen Beneath the Frost · Chapter 9 of 34

quests.title: Brambrake's Gate
quests.summary: An unseen territorial voice blocks the road north.

fields.overview: An unseen territorial voice blocks the road north.
fields.gameplayUse: Repeated story gate; do not reveal Brambrake's face until it opens.
fields.storyBeats:
An enormous gate cuts off the northern forest. Gwen argues with Brambrake, a stubborn resident who remains concealed on the other side and insists that everything beyond the barrier is 'his side.' He dismisses the insect crisis because it has not yet affected him.

The early scenes must not show Brambrake's portrait or face. His dry, antisocial voice and the absurd scale of his territorial claim carry the encounter. Gwen returns as the cold worsens and the distinction between his side and everyone else's becomes impossible to maintain. Only when he finally opens the gate does the story give him a proper visual reveal. The exact task that convinces him remains editable until confirmed by newer canon.
fields.objectives: The gate becomes the central story barrier between the cozy village region and the worsening northern crisis.
fields.connectedWorldbuilding: Gwen, Brambrake, Brambrake's Gate, Northern Whisker Woods
fields.chronology: Act I — The Queen Beneath the Frost · Chapter 10 of 34

quests.title: Bug Is on the Loose
quests.summary: An electric-insect investigation ends with a goblin-shaped misunderstanding.

fields.overview: An electric-insect investigation ends with a goblin-shaped misunderstanding.
fields.storyBeats:
During an insect crisis, villagers warn that 'Bug' attacked near the trail and left lightning damage behind. Gwen follows scorched bark and electrical residue, naturally assuming that another corrupted insect has gained elemental power.

The reveal is simpler and stranger: Bug is a goblin whose name is Bug. He uses lightning magic, but he is not an insect. The misunderstanding gives Act I a comedic release without making the disturbance irrelevant. Gwen may chase, fight, or bargain with him according to the existing quest, but the canonical point is the same: reports about an electric bug were reports about a lightning goblin named Bug.
fields.objectives: The mystery introduces goblins and lightning magic while puncturing the grim insect investigation with character comedy.
fields.connectedWorldbuilding: Gwen, Bug, Goblins, Whisker Woods, Lightning Magic
fields.chronology: Act I — The Queen Beneath the Frost · Chapter 11 of 34

quests.title: The Fire Meal
quests.summary: Tohm asks Gwen to cook a kind of meal that can change the person who eats it.

fields.overview: Tohm asks Gwen to cook a kind of meal that can change the person who eats it.
fields.storyBeats:
Tohm distinguishes Magical Meals from ordinary food, snacks, ales, and tonics. A Magical Meal does not merely restore the body or provide a brief buff; it can draw power, memory, and meaning out of ingredients and the person who prepares them. The Fire Meal is Gwen's first major encounter with that power.

Gwen gathers its ingredients through the same loop she has learned across Whisker Woods. The exact final recipe remains editable, but the finished dish radiates an unnatural heat. Tohm watches with the focus of someone who has waited years for this moment and warns Gwen that the meal may not behave like ordinary cooking. When Gwen tastes it, the tavern disappears.
fields.objectives: The food system crosses into the main mystery as Gwen enters her first trance.
fields.connectedWorldbuilding: Gwen, Tohm Kyatt, Fire Meal, Magical Meals, Tohm's Recipe Book
fields.chronology: Act I — The Queen Beneath the Frost · Chapter 12 of 34

quests.title: The First Trance
quests.summary: Fire carries Gwen into an impossible winter hidden inside Whisker Woods.

fields.overview: Fire carries Gwen into an impossible winter hidden inside Whisker Woods.
fields.storyBeats:
Gwen awakens inside a vision of Whisker Woods consumed by a snowstorm. The season is impossible. Frozen paths lead toward a cavernous hive filled with eggs, Crayhusks, beetles, and Dappleflies carrying frost across their bodies. When the insects attack, Gwen instinctively draws on the Fire Meal and discovers flame moving through her sword and strikes.

The trance is not a decorative dream. It has physical rules, hostile creatures, and geography that feels disturbingly specific. Gwen pushes through the hive until she hears a child singing somewhere beyond the storm. She follows the melody deeper into the memory.
fields.objectives: Gwen discovers fire abilities and receives the first supernatural image of the Act I finale.
fields.connectedWorldbuilding: Gwen, Fire Meal, Whisker Woods, Ice Queen's Hive, Crayhusks, Dappleflies
fields.chronology: Act I — The Queen Beneath the Frost · Chapter 13 of 34

quests.title: The Girl and the Creature
quests.summary: A child's kindness creates the trust that will later be exploited.

fields.overview: A child's kindness creates the trust that will later be exploited.
fields.storyBeats:
The song leads Gwen to a small girl in a purple nightgown carrying a stuffed faery doll. The child cannot see or hear her. In the shadows lies an enormous wounded insect-like creature, its true shape concealed by darkness and the limited perspective of the memory.

Instead of fearing the creature, the girl brings water and food, cleans its wound, comforts it, and sings. The creature trusts her. Searchers eventually call for a princess, but the trance ends before Gwen can identify either figure. At this point the Story Reader must preserve the same knowledge boundary as the game: the girl is not yet named as Lillia, and the creature is not yet named as the Ant Queen.
fields.objectives: The story establishes sincere childhood kindness before revealing how that relationship becomes the cause of the Ice Queen tragedy.
fields.connectedWorldbuilding: Gwen, Princess Lillia, Ant Queen, Fire Meal Trance, Faery Doll
fields.chronology: Act I — The Queen Beneath the Frost · Chapter 14 of 34

quests.title: Gwen Wakes
quests.summary: The tavern returns, but Tohm's reaction makes the vision more suspicious.

fields.overview: The tavern returns, but Tohm's reaction makes the vision more suspicious.
fields.storyBeats:
Gwen wakes in the tavern after collapsing, surrounded by scorch marks and frightened witnesses. Juno helps ground her while Gwen explains the frozen forest, the hive, the child, and the wounded creature.

Tohm's reaction is too controlled. He recognizes more than he admits, avoids direct answers, and redirects Gwen toward mastering the power before asking where it came from. The moment keeps him loving and protective without excusing his secrecy. Gwen still trusts her mentor, but the player can see the first clear evidence that he is withholding history connected to the meal.
fields.objectives: The Fire Meal becomes usable power, and suspicion of Tohm becomes part of Gwen's investigation.
fields.connectedWorldbuilding: Gwen, Tohm Kyatt, Juno, Fire Meal, First Trance
fields.chronology: Act I — The Queen Beneath the Frost · Chapter 15 of 34

quests.title: Learning the Fire Meal
quests.summary: Gwen turns a frightening vision into a controlled combat language.

fields.overview: Gwen turns a frightening vision into a controlled combat language.
fields.storyBeats:
Gwen begins learning what the Fire Meal can do: ignite her sword, apply burning damage, create explosive heat, resist cold, launch fire, or build toward a stronger finishing technique. The exact move set remains a gameplay decision, but the power must feel like an extension of cooking rather than an unrelated spell list.

Juno helps Gwen practice. Their second training sequence contrasts supernatural force with reliable fundamentals. Gwen can burn through barriers and overwhelm enemies, but poor timing still leaves her open. The lesson matters because the Ice Queen will eventually require both the meal's power and everything Gwen already knew as a fighter.
fields.objectives: New routes and combat options open while the story prepares the mechanical answer to the frozen north.
fields.connectedWorldbuilding: Gwen, Juno, Fire Meal, Magical Meal Combat
fields.chronology: Act I — The Queen Beneath the Frost · Chapter 16 of 34

quests.title: The North Grows Colder
quests.summary: The impossible winter begins crossing from Gwen's trance into reality.

fields.overview: The impossible winter begins crossing from Gwen's trance into reality.
fields.storyBeats:
Cold spreads through northern Whisker Woods. More insects appear, nests become denser, roots freeze, and ordinary creatures flee south. The details increasingly match the place Gwen saw in the Fire Meal trance.

Once Brambrake finally permits access through his gate, Gwen reaches caves whose frozen roots and egg chambers mirror the vision's geography. That recognition matters: the trance was connected to a real location and a real history, not a random nightmare. The investigation now has a direction beneath the forest.
fields.objectives: Brambrake's barrier opens and Gwen descends toward the organized insect colony.
fields.connectedWorldbuilding: Gwen, Northern Whisker Woods, Brambrake, Fire Meal Trance, Ice Queen's Hive
fields.chronology: Act I — The Queen Beneath the Frost · Chapter 17 of 34

quests.title: Thairrott
quests.summary: An ancient skeletal-root guardian blocks the route beneath the forest.

fields.overview: An ancient skeletal-root guardian blocks the route beneath the forest.
fields.storyBeats:
At the cavern entrance, Gwen confronts Thairrott, an enormous guardian formed from bones, roots, branches, and the disturbed remains of the old forest. Its final silhouette should follow the newest approved art, but its story function is fixed: it is the gatekeeper between the surface investigation and the colony beneath.

The fight asks Gwen to read slow, devastating patterns while using fire to create openings through rooted defenses. Defeating Thairrott does not solve the corruption. It breaks the seal on a much larger network of tunnels and proves that ancient forces beneath Whisker Woods have awakened with the insects.
fields.objectives: The path into the insect kingdom opens and the investigation becomes a descent into an organized society.
fields.connectedWorldbuilding: Gwen, Thairrott, Northern Cavern, Whisker Woods, Fire Meal
fields.chronology: Act I — The Queen Beneath the Frost · Chapter 18 of 34

quests.title: This Is Not an Infestation
quests.summary: The caverns reveal a kingdom with food, labor, and hierarchy.

fields.overview: The caverns reveal a kingdom with food, labor, and hierarchy.
fields.storyBeats:
Beyond Thairrott, the tunnels contain egg chambers, storage spaces, food routes, specialized workers, frozen nurseries, and defensive positions. The insects are not a mindless swarm. They belong to a functioning society with roles, logistics, and a ruler.

The corruption has distorted that society into an army, but evidence of its older purpose remains. Gwen begins to understand that clearing nests is not the same as exterminating vermin. Something central has changed the colony, and the creatures attacking the surface are symptoms of what happened to their Queen.
fields.objectives: The moral stakes shift from defeating pests to confronting the corruption of a people and their ruler.
fields.connectedWorldbuilding: Gwen, Ant Colony, Intelligent Insect Society, Ice Queen's Hive, Whisken People
fields.chronology: Act I — The Queen Beneath the Frost · Chapter 19 of 34

quests.title: Cedric the Grunt
quests.summary: A defeated skeleton guard turns survival into a business opportunity.

fields.overview: A defeated skeleton guard turns survival into a business opportunity.
fields.storyBeats:
Cedric is an armed skeletal grunt guarding the corrupted northern routes under orders he would rather not explain. He is bureaucratic, evasive, and dangerous enough to require a fight, but his courage evaporates once Gwen wins. Cedric surrenders and makes himself useful before she can decide what to do with him.

Gwen spares him, establishing that she does not treat every enemy-shaped person as irredeemable. Cedric becomes a recurring ally associated with Charms: selling, modifying, upgrading, and profiting from them with shameless enthusiasm. He can later trade his grunt helmet for a hooded look. His information also confirms that the insects have a Queen and that lately the Queen has become 'cold.'
fields.objectives: Gwen unlocks the recurring Charm relationship and receives direct confirmation that the colony's Queen has changed.
fields.connectedWorldbuilding: Gwen, Cedric the Grunt, Charms, Ice Queen, Ant Colony
fields.chronology: Act I — The Queen Beneath the Frost · Chapter 20 of 34

quests.title: Cedar, Lyra, and Oswin
quests.summary: Suspicious allies force Gwen to ask why Tohm's food resembles the corruption.

fields.overview: Suspicious allies force Gwen to ask why Tohm's food resembles the corruption.
fields.storyBeats:
Cedar and Lyra initially oppose Gwen because she carries Magical Meals made from Tohm's recipes while creatures across the north are being transformed by magical food. Their hostility is intelligent and defensive rather than evil. Once Gwen proves she is investigating the same danger, they bring her to Oswin, an older alchemist with enough knowledge to recognize a pattern.

Oswin listens to the pond, the boar, the caves, the Fire Meal, and the trance. Then he asks the questions Gwen has avoided: Where did Tohm learn these recipes? Why does the corruption resemble culinary magic? What did Tohm do before he became her mentor? Oswin does not reveal every answer, but he makes it impossible for Gwen to treat Tohm's secrecy as harmless eccentricity.
fields.objectives: Gwen gains allies and a framework for understanding the crisis as corrupted culinary magic.
fields.connectedWorldbuilding: Gwen, Cedar, Lyra, Oswin, Tohm Kyatt, Dark Culinary Arts
fields.chronology: Act I — The Queen Beneath the Frost · Chapter 21 of 34

quests.title: Corruption Through Consumption
quests.summary: The thing that nourishes Gwen is also being used to transform bodies, minds, and ecosystems.

fields.overview: The thing that nourishes Gwen is also being used to transform bodies, minds, and ecosystems.
fields.magicalEffect: Can corrupt, mutate, enslave, alter minds, transform bodies, and spread through ecosystems.
fields.storyFunction: Dark mirror of Gwen's food-based progression.
fields.storyBeats:
The evidence points to a consistent method: creatures are not changing merely because magic is nearby. They are eating Magical Meals, recipe fragments, concentrated ingredients, residue, or corrupted food created through the Dark Culinary Arts. Food can heal, comfort, strengthen, and unite, but the same intimacy makes it capable of mutation, control, addiction, and environmental spread.

An optional side story sharpens this discovery. A camp connected to Mu'Ramar is found destroyed, and Gwen survives a night encounter with a cursed were-creature who returns to human form at dawn. The victim says magical cookies caused the transformation, possibly distributed by Cedric without proper warning. The dates do not match Mu'Ramar's account, and Mu'Ramar disappears when Gwen notices. If newer canon contradicts this quest, it remains clearly marked as a soft-canon draft rather than being erased.
fields.objectives: Gwen understands the central danger of corrupted food and sees that it can transform people as well as wildlife.
fields.connectedWorldbuilding: Gwen, Dark Culinary Arts, Magical Meals, Mu'Ramar, Cedric the Grunt, Magical Cookies
fields.chronology: Act I — The Queen Beneath the Frost · Chapter 22 of 34

quests.title: The History of the Ant Queen
quests.summary: The Whisken once shared the forest with the colony rather than fighting it.

fields.overview: The Whisken once shared the forest with the colony rather than fighting it.
fields.storyBeats:
Gwen learns that an Ant Kingdom existed beneath Whisker Woods long before the current attacks. The Ant Queen and the Whisken eventually formed a relationship built around cultivation, food, cooperation, balance, and shared resources. The insects helped the forest thrive, while Whisken communities benefited from the abundance they supported.

One historical version says a gluttonous Ant King hoarded food while his colony suffered, and that the Queen allied with the Whisken to overthrow or seal him away. That portion remains soft canon until confirmed. The hard canon is the positive relationship between the Queen and the Whisken. It makes the modern violence tragic and echoes the Feast of Full Plates: food shared sustains a community; food hoarded or corrupted destroys one.
fields.objectives: The Ice Queen can no longer be understood as an inherently evil monster, and restoring the forest gains historical weight.
fields.connectedWorldbuilding: Ant Queen, Whisken People, Ant Colony, Whisker Woods, Feast of Full Plates, Gluttonous Ant King
