chapters.subtitle: Ovenhold and the Faery Realm forget how to share a table.
chapters.era: Ancient History
chapters.shortDescription: A devastating war between Ovenhold and the Faery Realm lasted for 300 years. The conflict shaped the world, exhausted both kingdoms, and created a hunger for peace that no army could satisfy.

pages.title: Two Kingdoms Divided
pages.text: Ovenhold was a mortal kingdom of hearths, ovens, labor, craft, survival, and cooked food. The Faery Realm was ancient, beautiful, proud, magical, and rooted in nature and spirit. Fear, hunger, pride, territory, and misunderstanding slowly turned both kingdoms away from hospitality and toward war.
pages.imagePlaceholder: A split kingdom map, half hearth-lit stonework and half luminous faery wood.
pages.caption: The first divide was not a border. It was a failure to sit together.

pages.title: Three Centuries of Hunger
pages.text: The war lasted 300 years. Generations were born into conflict, food became scarce, feasts vanished from memory, and even victory began to taste bitter. The damage was not only in the fields and forests. It reached the soul of hospitality itself.
pages.imagePlaceholder: A long banquet table with empty bowls, broken chairs, and cold ash.
pages.caption: A world can survive without victory longer than it can survive without bread.

pages.title: The World Waits for a Meal
pages.text: No sword, treaty, king, queen, army, or spell could end the war. Something else had to arrive. Something simple, impossible, and sacred: a meal prepared with Passion, Taste, and Love.
pages.imagePlaceholder: A tiny warm light appearing at the center of a battlefield.
pages.caption: Before peace had a name, it had a scent.

chapters.title: The Tablemaker's Arrival
chapters.subtitle: A stranger brings tools, ingredients, and a table.
chapters.era: Ancient History
chapters.shortDescription: A mysterious figure known as the Tablemaker arrived during the final years of the war. He did not come as a warrior, king, or mage. He came as one who could prepare a table for enemies.

pages.title: The Man Who Brought a Table
pages.text: The Tablemaker arrived with no army. He carried tools, ingredients, and a table. Ovenhold thought him foolish. The Faery Realm thought him small. Neither side understood that a table could be more dangerous to war than a blade.
pages.imagePlaceholder: A lone figure crossing a battlefield with a folded table on his back.
pages.caption: He did not ask who deserved peace. He prepared a place for it.

pages.title: A Feast Neither Side Could Refuse
pages.text: The Tablemaker began preparing a meal so extraordinary that its scent crossed camps, walls, rivers, and old grudges. Soldiers paused. Faeries listened. Kings and queens grew curious despite themselves.
pages.imagePlaceholder: Steam curling like golden ribbons through battlefield fog.
pages.caption: The aroma did what banners could not.

pages.title: The Meal That Ended the War
pages.text: The meal perfectly held Passion, Taste, and Love. Everyone who ate remembered what it meant to be alive, hungry, forgiven, and welcomed. The war did not end because anyone surrendered. It ended because everyone remembered the table.
pages.imagePlaceholder: Ovenhold and faery leaders sharing one impossible meal.
pages.caption: Peace began with a bite.

pages.title: The Cost of the Meal
pages.text: The meal was too powerful for a mortal body. The act of creating something so full of Food Essence, love, and divine culinary power killed the Tablemaker. His sacrifice became the sacred wound at the heart of magical cooking.
pages.imagePlaceholder: A fallen apron beside a glowing table.
pages.caption: The final ingredient was himself.

pages.title: Peace at the Same Table
pages.text: Ovenhold and the Faery Realm ended the war and became allies. Their alliance lasts to this day, not because they forgot their wounds, but because they shared a meal that made hatred impossible to swallow.
pages.imagePlaceholder: Two crowns resting on opposite sides of one table.
pages.caption: The treaty was written after the meal, but the meal made it true.

pages.title: The Culinary Beyond
pages.text: The Tablemaker did not truly vanish. His spirit returned to The Everfeast, a heavenly culinary realm where all meals are remembered in their perfect form. Before returning, he released a spirit of Food Essence into the world, helping form the foundation of magical cooking and the sacred nature of meals.
pages.imagePlaceholder: A doorway of warm light opening beyond an endless kitchen.
pages.caption: The Everfeast keeps every meal that ever healed someone.

chapters.title: Tohm Kyatt's Obsession
chapters.subtitle: Wonder curdles into hunger for the ultimate taste.
chapters.era: Pre-Game History
chapters.shortDescription: Centuries later, Tohm Kyatt grows fascinated with legends of impossible meals, the Tablemaker, and magical cooking. What begins as wonder slowly turns into obsession.

pages.title: The Cat Who Could Taste Sweetness
pages.text: Tohm Kyatt was a rare Whisken with an extraordinary relationship to taste. Sweetness did not simply please him. It opened doors in his mind. Every flavor became a question, and every meal became a clue.
pages.imagePlaceholder: Young Tohm studying a pastry like it is a map.
pages.caption: Some people taste food. Tohm investigated it.

pages.title: The Legend That Would Not Leave Him
pages.text: Tohm heard stories of the Tablemaker, The Everfeast, magical meals, and legendary recipes. The stories would not leave him. He became convinced that a meal like the Tablemaker's could be created again.
pages.imagePlaceholder: A recipe book open beside old faery tale illustrations.
pages.caption: A legend is harmless until someone mistakes it for a recipe.

pages.title: From Wonder to Hunger
pages.text: Ordinary food stopped satisfying him. Tohm did not simply want to cook. He wanted the ultimate taste, a flavor beyond memory, beyond safety, beyond the limits of a chef who still knew when to stop.
pages.imagePlaceholder: A kitchen full of perfect dishes, all ignored.
pages.caption: Wonder asks. Obsession demands.

pages.title: The First Dangerous Step
pages.text: Tohm began searching for magical tools and recipes. That search would one day pull him toward the Cat Cauldron, the Dragon Knife, the Recipe Book, and disasters he was not ready to name.
pages.imagePlaceholder: A shadowed cauldron, knife, and book arranged like warnings.
pages.caption: The road to disaster smelled wonderful at first.

chapters.title: Gwen Before the Tavern
chapters.subtitle: A practical fighter from Osul, not a chosen one.
chapters.era: Pre-Game History
chapters.shortDescription: Before Gwen becomes involved in Tohm's story, she lives as a hardworking, sharp, capable fighter from Osul.

pages.title: A Worker, Not a Chosen One
pages.text: Gwen was grounded and practical. She worked, gathered, fought, and survived. She was not waiting for prophecy. She paid attention, got things done, and protected what needed protecting.
pages.imagePlaceholder: Gwen carrying tools and a basket at the edge of a village path.
pages.caption: Her strength came from ordinary work done seriously.

pages.title: Osul and Ordinary Strength
pages.text: Life in Osul taught Gwen the value of food, labor, courage, and sharp judgment. She was not chasing legend. She was trying to live well, work hard, and keep danger from reaching the people around her.
pages.imagePlaceholder: A warm Osul workyard with tools, food baskets, and practice weapons.
pages.caption: Ordinary strength is still strength.

pages.title: The Kind of Person Tohm Needed
pages.text: Gwen was brave, smart, skilled, stubborn, and capable. That made her exactly the kind of person Tohm Kyatt needed, though whether Tohm deserved that help was another question entirely.
pages.imagePlaceholder: Gwen looking toward a strange tavern silhouette in the distance.
pages.caption: The right sous chef is sometimes the person who tells you no.

chapters.title: When Tohm Met Gwen
chapters.subtitle: A tavern job becomes the first step into the main story.
chapters.era: Beginning of the Game
chapters.shortDescription: Tohm Kyatt recruits Gwen, setting the playable story into motion. What seems like a simple tavern job becomes the beginning of a much larger journey.

pages.title: The Offer
pages.text: Tohm Kyatt approached Gwen with work connected to the Living Tavern. It sounded like a job. It felt like a test. With Tohm, those things were often the same.
pages.imagePlaceholder: Tohm making a dramatic offer outside the Living Tavern.
pages.caption: A chef, a fighter, and a door that would not stay ordinary.

pages.title: A Strange Chef and a Stranger Job
pages.text: Gwen quickly realized Tohm was brilliant, dramatic, secretive, and intense about food in a way that made normal questions feel too small. He needed help, but he was not saying everything.
pages.imagePlaceholder: A tavern kitchen filled with impossible tools and suspiciously glowing ingredients.
pages.caption: The job description did not mention mysteries.

pages.title: The Sous Chef
pages.text: Gwen became tied to the tavern's work. Gathering, cooking, fighting, helping, and learning became the rhythm of the game. She was not just hired into a kitchen. She was pulled into a story.
pages.imagePlaceholder: Gwen with a basket, sword, and cooking station.
pages.caption: A sous chef can save a world if the recipe is strange enough.

pages.title: The Road to Whisker Woods
pages.text: The road led toward Whisker Woods, where the first tasks seemed simple enough: gather ingredients, help people, learn the land, and notice what was beginning to go wrong.
pages.imagePlaceholder: A forest road under warm morning light, with the Living Tavern behind.
pages.caption: Every first act begins as a place to walk into.

chapters.title: The Stolen Recipes
chapters.subtitle: Torn pages start spreading dangerous powers.
chapters.era: Beginning of the Game
chapters.shortDescription: The Recipe Book is no longer whole. Torn pages are loose in the world, and corrupted cooking begins turning hunger, power, and ambition into threats.

pages.title: Pages in the Wrong Hands
pages.text: The Recipe Book held more than instructions. Its pages carried culinary power, history, and risk. When pages were torn loose, the recipes stopped belonging only to Tohm Kyatt.
pages.imagePlaceholder: Torn recipe pages drifting over a dark kitchen flame.
pages.caption: A recipe can be a promise or a weapon.

pages.title: Dark Culinary Arts
pages.text: Lillia's use of Dark Culinary Arts twists food into corruption. Meals that should nourish become tools of control, mutation, and fear. Gwen's recovery of recipe pages becomes more than cleanup. It becomes protection.
pages.imagePlaceholder: A beautiful dish with a dark aura cracking through it.
pages.caption: Not every meal wants to feed you.

chapters.title: The Final Test
chapters.subtitle: Gwen earns the title of chef before choosing where she belongs.
chapters.era: Act I — The Queen Beneath the Frost
chapters.shortDescription: Gwen earns the title of chef before choosing where she belongs.
chapters.overviewText: After roughly two years of practical apprenticeship under the legendary Whisken chef Tohm Kyatt, Gwen returns to the Culinary Imperial Academy of Unhold for the final stage of her education. The apprenticeship made her capable, but it did not make her officially qualified. To graduate, she must conceptualize, prepare, cook, and present a dish of her own design before the Academy judges.
chapters.developerNotes: Canon gap: confirm the final name and recipe of Gwen's examination dish. The Academy's Unhold/Ovenhold naming relationship also remains unresolved.

pages.title: The Final Test
pages.text:
After roughly two years of practical apprenticeship under the legendary Whisken chef Tohm Kyatt, Gwen returns to the Culinary Imperial Academy of Unhold for the final stage of her education. The apprenticeship made her capable, but it did not make her officially qualified. To graduate, she must conceptualize, prepare, cook, and present a dish of her own design before the Academy judges.

The test asks more than whether she can follow instructions. Gwen must show judgment, technique, and a culinary identity shaped by both formal Academy discipline and Tohm's improvisational teaching. The judges taste her dish and pass her. Gwen leaves the examination as a newly qualified chef, carrying proof that the difficult years away from home meant something. The final name and recipe of her graduation dish remain intentionally unresolved.

callouts.label: Player knowledge
callouts.text: Gwen has already completed her apprenticeship under Tohm and passes the Academy examination before the playable homecoming begins.

callouts.label: Story consequence
callouts.text: Gwen enters Act I as a qualified chef rather than a beginner, and her graduation dish becomes a symbol of her own culinary voice.

chapters.title: Gwen Chooses Home
chapters.subtitle: The Feast of Full Plates gives Gwen a choice between prestige and community.
chapters.era: Act I — The Queen Beneath the Frost
chapters.shortDescription: The Feast of Full Plates gives Gwen a choice between prestige and community.
chapters.overviewText: Gwen's qualification falls on the Feast of Full Plates, when the Academy and Ovenhold hold an enormous prestigious celebration. She could remain among celebrated chefs and enjoy the recognition she has earned. Instead, she leaves for Whisker Woods.

pages.title: Gwen Chooses Home
pages.text:
Gwen's qualification falls on the Feast of Full Plates, when the Academy and Ovenhold hold an enormous prestigious celebration. She could remain among celebrated chefs and enjoy the recognition she has earned. Instead, she leaves for Whisker Woods.

Gwen wants to spend the feast with Tohm, Juno, Kap, and the Whisken community that became her second home. The decision quietly defines her priorities. Prestige matters less than the people who fed her, trained her, argued with her, and gave her a place at their table. Whisker Woods is not merely where Tohm's tavern happens to stand. It is the community Gwen chooses.

callouts.label: Player knowledge
callouts.text: Gwen deliberately leaves the Academy celebration to return to Whisker Woods on the same day she qualifies.

callouts.label: Story consequence
callouts.text: Her homecoming and the sacred feast become one celebration, establishing community as Gwen's central motivation.

chapters.title: Something Is Wrong with Whisker Woods
chapters.subtitle: A familiar road shows the first signs of an organized corruption.
chapters.era: Act I — The Queen Beneath the Frost
chapters.shortDescription: A familiar road shows the first signs of an organized corruption.
chapters.overviewText: The path home should be familiar, but Whisker Woods feels wrong almost immediately. Insects appear in unusual numbers. Beetles and Dappleflies behave with unnatural aggression, egg clusters cling to places where they should not exist, and frightened wildlife has been pushed out of its normal territory.

pages.title: Something Is Wrong with Whisker Woods
pages.text:
The path home should be familiar, but Whisker Woods feels wrong almost immediately. Insects appear in unusual numbers. Beetles and Dappleflies behave with unnatural aggression, egg clusters cling to places where they should not exist, and frightened wildlife has been pushed out of its normal territory.

The signs do not yet form a complete answer, but they are too consistent to dismiss as a bad season. Something is disturbing the forest's food chain and directing creatures that should be scattered. When Gwen hears Kap screaming from the direction of his pond, the unease becomes an immediate crisis.

callouts.label: Player knowledge
callouts.text: The forest's insects and wildlife are behaving unnaturally, but Gwen does not yet know the cause.

callouts.label: Story consequence
callouts.text: Gwen's homecoming becomes an investigation before she even reaches the feast.

chapters.title: Kap's Corrupted Pond
chapters.subtitle: Gwen's first day as a chef becomes her first rescue.
chapters.era: Act I — The Queen Beneath the Frost
chapters.shortDescription: Gwen's first day as a chef becomes her first rescue.
chapters.overviewText: Gwen reaches Kap's Pond and finds its water darkened by corruption, its vegetation dying, and its banks crowded with hostile insects. Kap is trapped near damaged fishing gear while bugs close around him. Gwen fights through the swarm to reach him, only for the disturbed water to erupt beneath them.

pages.title: Kap's Corrupted Pond
pages.text:
Gwen reaches Kap's Pond and finds its water darkened by corruption, its vegetation dying, and its banks crowded with hostile insects. Kap is trapped near damaged fishing gear while bugs close around him. Gwen fights through the swarm to reach him, only for the disturbed water to erupt beneath them.

A giant corrupted Prawnhusk rises from the pond. The armored creature turns the rescue into Gwen's first major combat test after returning home. She reads its heavy claw attacks, survives its territorial charges, and defeats it long enough to get Kap to safety. The victory proves Gwen can protect this community, but the residue around the creature makes one fact unavoidable: the forest is not suffering from an ordinary infestation.

callouts.label: Player knowledge
callouts.text: Kap's pond and the Prawnhusk have been altered by the same spreading corruption.

callouts.label: Story consequence
callouts.text: Kap is saved, while the Prawnhusk provides the first undeniable evidence that the forest itself is being changed.

chapters.title: Feast of Full Plates
chapters.subtitle: A sacred community feast becomes Gwen's homecoming and graduation celebration.
chapters.era: Act I — The Queen Beneath the Frost
chapters.shortDescription: A sacred community feast becomes Gwen's homecoming and graduation celebration.
chapters.overviewText: Gwen reaches the village after nightfall and finds Tohm's tavern overflowing with lantern light, music, food, and Whisken families. The Feast of Full Plates celebrates food shared rather than hoarded: hospitality, gratitude, abundance, reconciliation, and the promise that no one at the table should remain hungry. This year it also celebrates Gwen's return as a qualified chef.

pages.title: Feast of Full Plates
pages.text:
Gwen reaches the village after nightfall and finds Tohm's tavern overflowing with lantern light, music, food, and Whisken families. The Feast of Full Plates celebrates food shared rather than hoarded: hospitality, gratitude, abundance, reconciliation, and the promise that no one at the table should remain hungry. This year it also celebrates Gwen's return as a qualified chef.

Tohm's first response is a dry, 'You're late.' Kap's account of the pond and Prawnhusk finally earns Gwen his full attention. Tohm examines her Academy qualification with rare visible pride, then immediately puts her to work. Because he missed the examination, he asks Gwen to recreate the dish that earned her qualification. As they cook side by side, villagers trade rumors about lost produce, insect nests, dangerous roads, and frost appearing in the wrong season. Gwen notices that Tohm reacts to the mention of the cold before hiding it.

callouts.label: Player knowledge
callouts.text: The feast is both a holy communal celebration and Gwen's graduation homecoming; Tohm appears to recognize something in the reports of unnatural frost.

callouts.label: Story consequence
callouts.text: Gwen is welcomed home, her identity as a chef is affirmed, and Tohm's first suspicious reaction plants doubt beneath the warmth.

chapters.title: Juno's Friendly Fight
chapters.subtitle: A familiar sparring partner tests whether Gwen's long training dulled her instincts.
chapters.era: Act I — The Queen Beneath the Frost
chapters.shortDescription: A familiar sparring partner tests whether Gwen's long training dulled her instincts.
chapters.overviewText: Juno challenges Gwen to a friendly spar rather than a hostile duel. Their teasing makes it clear that this is a familiar language between friends: competitive, affectionate, and sharp enough that neither can be careless.

pages.title: Juno's Friendly Fight
pages.text:
Juno challenges Gwen to a friendly spar rather than a hostile duel. Their teasing makes it clear that this is a familiar language between friends: competitive, affectionate, and sharp enough that neither can be careless.

Juno blocks, dodges, punishes reckless attacks, and forces Gwen to think about spacing and timing. The encounter teaches the player combat fundamentals without pretending Gwen has never held a sword. She is already a capable fighter. Later, when the Fire Meal gives Gwen supernatural power, Juno serves the same purpose again by reminding her that flames cannot replace discipline.

callouts.label: Player knowledge
callouts.text: Juno is Gwen's trusted friend and capable training partner, not an enemy.

callouts.label: Story consequence
callouts.text: The player learns Gwen's baseline combat before Magical Meals alter it.

chapters.title: Life as a Chef in Whisker Woods
chapters.subtitle: The game's everyday loop grows naturally from Gwen's place in the tavern.
chapters.era: Act I — The Queen Beneath the Frost
chapters.shortDescription: The game's everyday loop grows naturally from Gwen's place in the tavern.
chapters.overviewText: For a time, Gwen settles into the work she returned to do. Tohm needs ingredients, so she explores, gathers, hunts, fights, and brings food home to cook. Turnips, herbs, Sunchee, Purfox, fruit, meat, and slime-derived ingredients make the forest feel like a living pantry rather than a corridor between battles.

pages.title: Life as a Chef in Whisker Woods
pages.text:
For a time, Gwen settles into the work she returned to do. Tohm needs ingredients, so she explores, gathers, hunts, fights, and brings food home to cook. Turnips, herbs, Sunchee, Purfox, fruit, meat, and slime-derived ingredients make the forest feel like a living pantry rather than a corridor between battles.

The routine introduces ordinary meals, healing ales and tonics, and smaller snacks that provide temporary strength, stamina, recovery, resistance, or mobility before Gwen ever masters a Magical Meal. Slimes belong to the food ecosystem as sources of flavor and substitution, with different gels supporting recipes and consumables. Gwen's complicated history with ale remains part of her character, but it does not reduce every tavern interaction to that struggle. The cozy loop gives the spreading corruption something meaningful to threaten.

callouts.label: Player knowledge
callouts.text: Gathering, cooking, and combat are parts of Gwen's normal responsibilities, while subtle corruption signs continue between errands.

callouts.label: Story consequence
callouts.text: The player learns the food-and-adventure loop and develops a practical reason to care about the forest's health.

chapters.title: The Magical Boar
chapters.subtitle: A hunt proves that the corruption is moving through what creatures consume.
chapters.era: Act I — The Queen Beneath the Frost
chapters.shortDescription: A hunt proves that the corruption is moving through what creatures consume.
chapters.overviewText: A search for stronger ingredients leads Gwen to a boar that has become unnaturally powerful. The animal charges hard enough to break trees and forces Gwen to rely on timing, positioning, and patience rather than simple aggression.

pages.title: The Magical Boar
pages.text:
A search for stronger ingredients leads Gwen to a boar that has become unnaturally powerful. The animal charges hard enough to break trees and forces Gwen to rely on timing, positioning, and patience rather than simple aggression.

When it falls, Gwen finds magical residue associated with what the boar consumed. The encounter advances the culinary progression — better and stranger ingredients can create stronger food — while revealing its dark mirror. The forest's food chain is being poisoned or manipulated, and creatures are changing because of what enters their bodies.

callouts.label: Player knowledge
callouts.text: The boar's transformation is linked to consumed magical residue rather than natural mutation.

callouts.label: Story consequence
callouts.text: Gwen gains a rare ingredient and the investigation shifts toward food as the mechanism of corruption.

chapters.title: The Academy Rival
chapters.subtitle: A Cook Battle measures what Tohm's apprenticeship added to Gwen's formal training.
chapters.era: Act I — The Queen Beneath the Frost
chapters.shortDescription: A Cook Battle measures what Tohm's apprenticeship added to Gwen's formal training.
chapters.overviewText: A former Academy classmate challenges Gwen to a Cook Battle. The rival is competitive but not hateful: she understands Gwen's stubbornness, recognizes the influence of Tohm's teaching, and favors precision and formal technique over wilderness improvisation.
chapters.developerNotes: Do not finalize Ressa Vale as the character's name without explicit confirmation.

pages.title: The Academy Rival
pages.text:
A former Academy classmate challenges Gwen to a Cook Battle. The rival is competitive but not hateful: she understands Gwen's stubbornness, recognizes the influence of Tohm's teaching, and favors precision and formal technique over wilderness improvisation.

The competition tests Taste, Technique, and Presentation through ingredient choice, heat, preparation, seasoning, timing, recovery, and risk. The rival initially dismisses one of Gwen's slime-derived substitutions as crude. Gwen makes it work by combining Academy discipline with the adaptability she learned in Whisker Woods. The result proves that her years under Tohm did not interrupt her education; they completed a missing part of it. The rival or nearby caravan also brings news of unnatural frost along the northern road. Her canonical name remains Academy Rival — Name TBD; Ressa Vale is only a retired working-name note.

callouts.label: Player knowledge
callouts.text: The rival respects Gwen even while challenging her, and the northern frost is spreading beyond isolated forest pockets.

callouts.label: Story consequence
callouts.text: Gwen proves her hybrid cooking style and receives another clue pointing north.

chapters.title: Brambrake's Gate
chapters.subtitle: An unseen territorial voice blocks the road north.
chapters.era: Act I — The Queen Beneath the Frost
chapters.shortDescription: An unseen territorial voice blocks the road north.
chapters.overviewText: An enormous gate cuts off the northern forest. Gwen argues with Brambrake, a stubborn resident who remains concealed on the other side and insists that everything beyond the barrier is 'his side.' He dismisses the insect crisis because it has not yet affected him.
chapters.developerNotes: Canon gap: confirm the final gate-opening quest. Never reveal Brambrake's face during the early gate exchanges.

pages.title: Brambrake's Gate
pages.text:
An enormous gate cuts off the northern forest. Gwen argues with Brambrake, a stubborn resident who remains concealed on the other side and insists that everything beyond the barrier is 'his side.' He dismisses the insect crisis because it has not yet affected him.

The early scenes must not show Brambrake's portrait or face. His dry, antisocial voice and the absurd scale of his territorial claim carry the encounter. Gwen returns as the cold worsens and the distinction between his side and everyone else's becomes impossible to maintain. Only when he finally opens the gate does the story give him a proper visual reveal. The exact task that convinces him remains editable until confirmed by newer canon.

callouts.label: Player knowledge
callouts.text: Brambrake controls access to the north, but his appearance is deliberately hidden until he allows Gwen through.

callouts.label: Story consequence
callouts.text: The gate becomes the central story barrier between the cozy village region and the worsening northern crisis.

chapters.title: Bug Is on the Loose
chapters.subtitle: An electric-insect investigation ends with a goblin-shaped misunderstanding.
chapters.era: Act I — The Queen Beneath the Frost
chapters.shortDescription: An electric-insect investigation ends with a goblin-shaped misunderstanding.
chapters.overviewText: During an insect crisis, villagers warn that 'Bug' attacked near the trail and left lightning damage behind. Gwen follows scorched bark and electrical residue, naturally assuming that another corrupted insect has gained elemental power.

pages.title: Bug Is on the Loose
pages.text:
During an insect crisis, villagers warn that 'Bug' attacked near the trail and left lightning damage behind. Gwen follows scorched bark and electrical residue, naturally assuming that another corrupted insect has gained elemental power.

The reveal is simpler and stranger: Bug is a goblin whose name is Bug. He uses lightning magic, but he is not an insect. The misunderstanding gives Act I a comedic release without making the disturbance irrelevant. Gwen may chase, fight, or bargain with him according to the existing quest, but the canonical point is the same: reports about an electric bug were reports about a lightning goblin named Bug.

callouts.label: Player knowledge
callouts.text: Bug is a goblin character and must never be filed as an insect enemy.

callouts.label: Story consequence
callouts.text: The mystery introduces goblins and lightning magic while puncturing the grim insect investigation with character comedy.

chapters.title: The Fire Meal
chapters.subtitle: Tohm asks Gwen to cook a kind of meal that can change the person who eats it.
chapters.era: Act I — The Queen Beneath the Frost
chapters.shortDescription: Tohm asks Gwen to cook a kind of meal that can change the person who eats it.
chapters.overviewText: Tohm distinguishes Magical Meals from ordinary food, snacks, ales, and tonics. A Magical Meal does not merely restore the body or provide a brief buff; it can draw power, memory, and meaning out of ingredients and the person who prepares them. The Fire Meal is Gwen's first major encounter with that power.

pages.title: The Fire Meal
pages.text:
Tohm distinguishes Magical Meals from ordinary food, snacks, ales, and tonics. A Magical Meal does not merely restore the body or provide a brief buff; it can draw power, memory, and meaning out of ingredients and the person who prepares them. The Fire Meal is Gwen's first major encounter with that power.

Gwen gathers its ingredients through the same loop she has learned across Whisker Woods. The exact final recipe remains editable, but the finished dish radiates an unnatural heat. Tohm watches with the focus of someone who has waited years for this moment and warns Gwen that the meal may not behave like ordinary cooking. When Gwen tastes it, the tavern disappears.

callouts.label: Player knowledge
callouts.text: Tohm understands Magical Meals far more deeply than he has explained, and the Fire Meal is different from every consumable introduced so far.

callouts.label: Story consequence
callouts.text: The food system crosses into the main mystery as Gwen enters her first trance.

chapters.title: The First Trance
chapters.subtitle: Fire carries Gwen into an impossible winter hidden inside Whisker Woods.
chapters.era: Act I — The Queen Beneath the Frost
chapters.shortDescription: Fire carries Gwen into an impossible winter hidden inside Whisker Woods.
chapters.overviewText: Gwen awakens inside a vision of Whisker Woods consumed by a snowstorm. The season is impossible. Frozen paths lead toward a cavernous hive filled with eggs, Crayhusks, beetles, and Dappleflies carrying frost across their bodies. When the insects attack, Gwen instinctively draws on the Fire Meal and discovers flame moving through her sword and strikes.

pages.title: The First Trance
pages.text:
Gwen awakens inside a vision of Whisker Woods consumed by a snowstorm. The season is impossible. Frozen paths lead toward a cavernous hive filled with eggs, Crayhusks, beetles, and Dappleflies carrying frost across their bodies. When the insects attack, Gwen instinctively draws on the Fire Meal and discovers flame moving through her sword and strikes.

The trance is not a decorative dream. It has physical rules, hostile creatures, and geography that feels disturbingly specific. Gwen pushes through the hive until she hears a child singing somewhere beyond the storm. She follows the melody deeper into the memory.

callouts.label: Player knowledge
callouts.text: Neither Gwen nor the player knows whether the snowstorm is a future, memory, or magical warning, and the identities at its center remain hidden.

callouts.label: Story consequence
callouts.text: Gwen discovers fire abilities and receives the first supernatural image of the Act I finale.

chapters.title: The Girl and the Creature
chapters.subtitle: A child's kindness creates the trust that will later be exploited.
chapters.era: Act I — The Queen Beneath the Frost
chapters.shortDescription: A child's kindness creates the trust that will later be exploited.
chapters.overviewText: The song leads Gwen to a small girl in a purple nightgown carrying a stuffed faery doll. The child cannot see or hear her. In the shadows lies an enormous wounded insect-like creature, its true shape concealed by darkness and the limited perspective of the memory.

pages.title: The Girl and the Creature
pages.text:
The song leads Gwen to a small girl in a purple nightgown carrying a stuffed faery doll. The child cannot see or hear her. In the shadows lies an enormous wounded insect-like creature, its true shape concealed by darkness and the limited perspective of the memory.

Instead of fearing the creature, the girl brings water and food, cleans its wound, comforts it, and sings. The creature trusts her. Searchers eventually call for a princess, but the trance ends before Gwen can identify either figure. At this point the Story Reader must preserve the same knowledge boundary as the game: the girl is not yet named as Lillia, and the creature is not yet named as the Ant Queen.

callouts.label: Player knowledge
callouts.text: Gwen sees a young princess and a shadowed giant insect, but does not yet know their names or future roles.

callouts.label: Story consequence
callouts.text: The story establishes sincere childhood kindness before revealing how that relationship becomes the cause of the Ice Queen tragedy.

chapters.title: Gwen Wakes
chapters.subtitle: The tavern returns, but Tohm's reaction makes the vision more suspicious.
chapters.era: Act I — The Queen Beneath the Frost
chapters.shortDescription: The tavern returns, but Tohm's reaction makes the vision more suspicious.
chapters.overviewText: Gwen wakes in the tavern after collapsing, surrounded by scorch marks and frightened witnesses. Juno helps ground her while Gwen explains the frozen forest, the hive, the child, and the wounded creature.

pages.title: Gwen Wakes
pages.text:
Gwen wakes in the tavern after collapsing, surrounded by scorch marks and frightened witnesses. Juno helps ground her while Gwen explains the frozen forest, the hive, the child, and the wounded creature.

Tohm's reaction is too controlled. He recognizes more than he admits, avoids direct answers, and redirects Gwen toward mastering the power before asking where it came from. The moment keeps him loving and protective without excusing his secrecy. Gwen still trusts her mentor, but the player can see the first clear evidence that he is withholding history connected to the meal.

callouts.label: Player knowledge
callouts.text: Tohm appears to recognize details from Gwen's trance even though he refuses to explain them.

callouts.label: Story consequence
callouts.text: The Fire Meal becomes usable power, and suspicion of Tohm becomes part of Gwen's investigation.

chapters.title: Learning the Fire Meal
chapters.subtitle: Gwen turns a frightening vision into a controlled combat language.
chapters.era: Act I — The Queen Beneath the Frost
chapters.shortDescription: Gwen turns a frightening vision into a controlled combat language.
chapters.overviewText: Gwen begins learning what the Fire Meal can do: ignite her sword, apply burning damage, create explosive heat, resist cold, launch fire, or build toward a stronger finishing technique. The exact move set remains a gameplay decision, but the power must feel like an extension of cooking rather than an unrelated spell list.

pages.title: Learning the Fire Meal
pages.text:
Gwen begins learning what the Fire Meal can do: ignite her sword, apply burning damage, create explosive heat, resist cold, launch fire, or build toward a stronger finishing technique. The exact move set remains a gameplay decision, but the power must feel like an extension of cooking rather than an unrelated spell list.

Juno helps Gwen practice. Their second training sequence contrasts supernatural force with reliable fundamentals. Gwen can burn through barriers and overwhelm enemies, but poor timing still leaves her open. The lesson matters because the Ice Queen will eventually require both the meal's power and everything Gwen already knew as a fighter.

callouts.label: Player knowledge
callouts.text: Fire is powerful but temporary and cannot replace Gwen's ordinary fighting skill.

callouts.label: Story consequence
callouts.text: New routes and combat options open while the story prepares the mechanical answer to the frozen north.

chapters.title: The North Grows Colder
chapters.subtitle: The impossible winter begins crossing from Gwen's trance into reality.
chapters.era: Act I — The Queen Beneath the Frost
chapters.shortDescription: The impossible winter begins crossing from Gwen's trance into reality.
chapters.overviewText: Cold spreads through northern Whisker Woods. More insects appear, nests become denser, roots freeze, and ordinary creatures flee south. The details increasingly match the place Gwen saw in the Fire Meal trance.

pages.title: The North Grows Colder
pages.text:
Cold spreads through northern Whisker Woods. More insects appear, nests become denser, roots freeze, and ordinary creatures flee south. The details increasingly match the place Gwen saw in the Fire Meal trance.

Once Brambrake finally permits access through his gate, Gwen reaches caves whose frozen roots and egg chambers mirror the vision's geography. That recognition matters: the trance was connected to a real location and a real history, not a random nightmare. The investigation now has a direction beneath the forest.

callouts.label: Player knowledge
callouts.text: The physical north confirms that Gwen's vision showed a real place connected to the present corruption.

callouts.label: Story consequence
callouts.text: Brambrake's barrier opens and Gwen descends toward the organized insect colony.

chapters.title: Thairrott
chapters.subtitle: An ancient skeletal-root guardian blocks the route beneath the forest.
chapters.era: Act I — The Queen Beneath the Frost
chapters.shortDescription: An ancient skeletal-root guardian blocks the route beneath the forest.
chapters.overviewText: At the cavern entrance, Gwen confronts Thairrott, an enormous guardian formed from bones, roots, branches, and the disturbed remains of the old forest. Its final silhouette should follow the newest approved art, but its story function is fixed: it is the gatekeeper between the surface investigation and the colony beneath.

pages.title: Thairrott
pages.text:
At the cavern entrance, Gwen confronts Thairrott, an enormous guardian formed from bones, roots, branches, and the disturbed remains of the old forest. Its final silhouette should follow the newest approved art, but its story function is fixed: it is the gatekeeper between the surface investigation and the colony beneath.

The fight asks Gwen to read slow, devastating patterns while using fire to create openings through rooted defenses. Defeating Thairrott does not solve the corruption. It breaks the seal on a much larger network of tunnels and proves that ancient forces beneath Whisker Woods have awakened with the insects.

callouts.label: Player knowledge
callouts.text: Thairrott is a guardian of the route into the colony, not the source of the crisis.

callouts.label: Story consequence
callouts.text: The path into the insect kingdom opens and the investigation becomes a descent into an organized society.

chapters.title: This Is Not an Infestation
chapters.subtitle: The caverns reveal a kingdom with food, labor, and hierarchy.
chapters.era: Act I — The Queen Beneath the Frost
chapters.shortDescription: The caverns reveal a kingdom with food, labor, and hierarchy.
chapters.overviewText: Beyond Thairrott, the tunnels contain egg chambers, storage spaces, food routes, specialized workers, frozen nurseries, and defensive positions. The insects are not a mindless swarm. They belong to a functioning society with roles, logistics, and a ruler.

pages.title: This Is Not an Infestation
pages.text:
Beyond Thairrott, the tunnels contain egg chambers, storage spaces, food routes, specialized workers, frozen nurseries, and defensive positions. The insects are not a mindless swarm. They belong to a functioning society with roles, logistics, and a ruler.

The corruption has distorted that society into an army, but evidence of its older purpose remains. Gwen begins to understand that clearing nests is not the same as exterminating vermin. Something central has changed the colony, and the creatures attacking the surface are symptoms of what happened to their Queen.

callouts.label: Player knowledge
callouts.text: The insects form an intelligent organized colony, and their current hostility is an altered state rather than their entire identity.

callouts.label: Story consequence
callouts.text: The moral stakes shift from defeating pests to confronting the corruption of a people and their ruler.

chapters.title: Cedric the Grunt
chapters.subtitle: A defeated skeleton guard turns survival into a business opportunity.
chapters.era: Act I — The Queen Beneath the Frost
chapters.shortDescription: A defeated skeleton guard turns survival into a business opportunity.
chapters.overviewText: Cedric is an armed skeletal grunt guarding the corrupted northern routes under orders he would rather not explain. He is bureaucratic, evasive, and dangerous enough to require a fight, but his courage evaporates once Gwen wins. Cedric surrenders and makes himself useful before she can decide what to do with him.

pages.title: Cedric the Grunt
pages.text:
Cedric is an armed skeletal grunt guarding the corrupted northern routes under orders he would rather not explain. He is bureaucratic, evasive, and dangerous enough to require a fight, but his courage evaporates once Gwen wins. Cedric surrenders and makes himself useful before she can decide what to do with him.

Gwen spares him, establishing that she does not treat every enemy-shaped person as irredeemable. Cedric becomes a recurring ally associated with Charms: selling, modifying, upgrading, and profiting from them with shameless enthusiasm. He can later trade his grunt helmet for a hooded look. His information also confirms that the insects have a Queen and that lately the Queen has become 'cold.'

callouts.label: Player knowledge
callouts.text: Cedric is an intelligent skeleton and opportunistic survivor, not a mindless undead monster.

callouts.label: Story consequence
callouts.text: Gwen unlocks the recurring Charm relationship and receives direct confirmation that the colony's Queen has changed.

chapters.title: Cedar, Lyra, and Oswin
chapters.subtitle: Suspicious allies force Gwen to ask why Tohm's food resembles the corruption.
chapters.era: Act I — The Queen Beneath the Frost
chapters.shortDescription: Suspicious allies force Gwen to ask why Tohm's food resembles the corruption.
chapters.overviewText: Cedar and Lyra initially oppose Gwen because she carries Magical Meals made from Tohm's recipes while creatures across the north are being transformed by magical food. Their hostility is intelligent and defensive rather than evil. Once Gwen proves she is investigating the same danger, they bring her to Oswin, an older alchemist with enough knowledge to recognize a pattern.

pages.title: Cedar, Lyra, and Oswin
pages.text:
Cedar and Lyra initially oppose Gwen because she carries Magical Meals made from Tohm's recipes while creatures across the north are being transformed by magical food. Their hostility is intelligent and defensive rather than evil. Once Gwen proves she is investigating the same danger, they bring her to Oswin, an older alchemist with enough knowledge to recognize a pattern.

Oswin listens to the pond, the boar, the caves, the Fire Meal, and the trance. Then he asks the questions Gwen has avoided: Where did Tohm learn these recipes? Why does the corruption resemble culinary magic? What did Tohm do before he became her mentor? Oswin does not reveal every answer, but he makes it impossible for Gwen to treat Tohm's secrecy as harmless eccentricity.

callouts.label: Player knowledge
callouts.text: Cedar, Lyra, and Oswin distrust Tohm's connection to magical food, but they do not yet possess his full hidden history.

callouts.label: Story consequence
callouts.text: Gwen gains allies and a framework for understanding the crisis as corrupted culinary magic.

chapters.title: Corruption Through Consumption
chapters.subtitle: The thing that nourishes Gwen is also being used to transform bodies, minds, and ecosystems.
chapters.era: Act I — The Queen Beneath the Frost
chapters.shortDescription: The thing that nourishes Gwen is also being used to transform bodies, minds, and ecosystems.
chapters.overviewText: The evidence points to a consistent method: creatures are not changing merely because magic is nearby. They are eating Magical Meals, recipe fragments, concentrated ingredients, residue, or corrupted food created through the Dark Culinary Arts. Food can heal, comfort, strengthen, and unite, but the same intimacy makes it capable of mutation, control, addiction, and environmental spread.
chapters.developerNotes: Mu'Ramar and the were-creature remain optional/soft canon if they conflict with newer records.

pages.title: Corruption Through Consumption
pages.text:
The evidence points to a consistent method: creatures are not changing merely because magic is nearby. They are eating Magical Meals, recipe fragments, concentrated ingredients, residue, or corrupted food created through the Dark Culinary Arts. Food can heal, comfort, strengthen, and unite, but the same intimacy makes it capable of mutation, control, addiction, and environmental spread.

An optional side story sharpens this discovery. A camp connected to Mu'Ramar is found destroyed, and Gwen survives a night encounter with a cursed were-creature who returns to human form at dawn. The victim says magical cookies caused the transformation, possibly distributed by Cedric without proper warning. The dates do not match Mu'Ramar's account, and Mu'Ramar disappears when Gwen notices. If newer canon contradicts this quest, it remains clearly marked as a soft-canon draft rather than being erased.

callouts.label: Player knowledge
callouts.text: Corruption spreads through consumption. The Mu'Ramar cookie story is optional soft canon pending timeline confirmation.

callouts.label: Story consequence
callouts.text: Gwen understands the central danger of corrupted food and sees that it can transform people as well as wildlife.

chapters.title: The History of the Ant Queen
chapters.subtitle: The Whisken once shared the forest with the colony rather than fighting it.
chapters.era: Act I — The Queen Beneath the Frost
chapters.shortDescription: The Whisken once shared the forest with the colony rather than fighting it.
chapters.overviewText: Gwen learns that an Ant Kingdom existed beneath Whisker Woods long before the current attacks. The Ant Queen and the Whisken eventually formed a relationship built around cultivation, food, cooperation, balance, and shared resources. The insects helped the forest thrive, while Whisken communities benefited from the abundance they supported.
chapters.developerNotes: Keep the Mad/Gluttonous Ant King marked Soft Canon unless later material confirms him.

pages.title: The History of the Ant Queen
pages.text:
Gwen learns that an Ant Kingdom existed beneath Whisker Woods long before the current attacks. The Ant Queen and the Whisken eventually formed a relationship built around cultivation, food, cooperation, balance, and shared resources. The insects helped the forest thrive, while Whisken communities benefited from the abundance they supported.

One historical version says a gluttonous Ant King hoarded food while his colony suffered, and that the Queen allied with the Whisken to overthrow or seal him away. That portion remains soft canon until confirmed. The hard canon is the positive relationship between the Queen and the Whisken. It makes the modern violence tragic and echoes the Feast of Full Plates: food shared sustains a community; food hoarded or corrupted destroys one.

callouts.label: Player knowledge
callouts.text: The Ant Queen and Whisken were once allies; the Gluttonous Ant King version remains a historical draft.

callouts.label: Story consequence
callouts.text: The Ice Queen can no longer be understood as an inherently evil monster, and restoring the forest gains historical weight.

chapters.title: The Blizzard
chapters.subtitle: The corruption stops hiding and turns northern Whisker Woods into winter.
chapters.era: Act I — The Queen Beneath the Frost
chapters.shortDescription: The corruption stops hiding and turns northern Whisker Woods into winter.
chapters.overviewText: A full magical blizzard consumes the north. Trees freeze, streams stop, frost-covered insects pour from the ground, and the season itself bends around the colony. The environmental corruption that first appeared in Kap's Pond is now visible across the region.

pages.title: The Blizzard
pages.text:
A full magical blizzard consumes the north. Trees freeze, streams stop, frost-covered insects pour from the ground, and the season itself bends around the colony. The environmental corruption that first appeared in Kap's Pond is now visible across the region.

Gwen follows the spread back toward the Queen at the center of the hive. The evidence points to one conclusion: the ancient Ant Queen has been transformed into the Ice Queen. What remains unknown is who changed her and why she accepted the meal that carried the corruption.

callouts.label: Player knowledge
callouts.text: The Ice Queen is the transformed ruler at the center of the colony, but the person responsible has not yet been identified.

callouts.label: Story consequence
callouts.text: The regional mystery becomes an open magical disaster and forces Tohm to surrender part of the truth.

chapters.title: Tohm Finally Says the Name
chapters.subtitle: The unnamed princess in Gwen's vision becomes Princess Lillia of Ovenhold.
chapters.era: Act I — The Queen Beneath the Frost
chapters.shortDescription: The unnamed princess in Gwen's vision becomes Princess Lillia of Ovenhold.
chapters.overviewText: Gwen confronts Tohm with the insects, the Queen, the corrupted meals, the frozen forest, and the child in her trance. Pressed beyond another deflection, Tohm finally gives her a name: Lillia, Princess of Ovenhold.

pages.title: Tohm Finally Says the Name
pages.text:
Gwen confronts Tohm with the insects, the Queen, the corrupted meals, the frozen forest, and the child in her trance. Pressed beyond another deflection, Tohm finally gives her a name: Lillia, Princess of Ovenhold.

Lillia grew up fascinated by faeries. Because humans and faeries share the greater Triad order, faeries were not distant monsters but a living people whose culture and magic she could admire. Admiration became obsession. Lillia wanted not merely to know faeries but to become one and possess magic. Her father, the King of Ovenhold, loved her intensely and tried to satisfy that desire. His disordered love eventually drove him to war with the Dwarven Kingdom for the Dragon Knife. Tohm's royal culinary access later placed that stolen artifact and his own dangerous obsession in the same story.

callouts.label: Player knowledge
callouts.text: The child from the trance is now identified as Lillia, but Gwen still does not know the full history of Tohm's dish or the torn pages.

callouts.label: Story consequence
callouts.text: Act I's local corruption connects to royal history, the Dragon Knife war, and Tohm's concealed past.

chapters.title: Lillia and the Ant Queen
chapters.subtitle: The first trance is reinterpreted as a real memory of compassion.
chapters.era: Act I — The Queen Beneath the Frost
chapters.shortDescription: The first trance is reinterpreted as a real memory of compassion.
chapters.overviewText: When Lillia was young, she became separated from her attendants in Whisker Woods and found the Ant Queen wounded. She stayed. She brought food and water, cleaned the wound, offered comfort, and sang while the enormous creature rested. The Queen remembered the child who treated her as a life worth saving rather than a monster.

pages.title: Lillia and the Ant Queen
pages.text:
When Lillia was young, she became separated from her attendants in Whisker Woods and found the Ant Queen wounded. She stayed. She brought food and water, cleaned the wound, offered comfort, and sang while the enormous creature rested. The Queen remembered the child who treated her as a life worth saving rather than a monster.

The shadowed creature in Gwen's trance was the Ant Queen, and the girl in the purple nightgown was Lillia. This kindness must remain genuine. Lillia was not born as a simple villain, and the Queen's later trust was not foolish. Their bond was formed through a real moment of mercy, which is precisely why its exploitation is so destructive.

callouts.label: Player knowledge
callouts.text: The story now confirms both identities from the trance and explains why the Queen trusted Lillia.

callouts.label: Story consequence
callouts.text: The emotional cause of the Ice Queen's transformation becomes clear before the mechanics of the corrupted meal are revealed.

chapters.title: The Meal That Created the Ice Queen
chapters.subtitle: Lillia returns with stolen culinary power and turns remembered kindness into access.
chapters.era: Act I — The Queen Beneath the Frost
chapters.shortDescription: Lillia returns with stolen culinary power and turns remembered kindness into access.
chapters.overviewText: Years after caring for the wounded Queen, Lillia returns with dangerous magic and torn pages from Tohm's recipe book. Tohm had used the Dragon Knife and forbidden culinary knowledge to create an unstable meal that gave Lillia power. When she tried to take his book, he recovered the main volume, but she tore out pages that became the foundation of the Dark Culinary Arts.
chapters.developerNotes: Use Blizzard Meal unless a newer canonical Ice Meal name is confirmed.

pages.title: The Meal That Created the Ice Queen
pages.text:
Years after caring for the wounded Queen, Lillia returns with dangerous magic and torn pages from Tohm's recipe book. Tohm had used the Dragon Knife and forbidden culinary knowledge to create an unstable meal that gave Lillia power. When she tried to take his book, he recovered the main volume, but she tore out pages that became the foundation of the Dark Culinary Arts.

Lillia brings the Ant Queen a corrupted ice-associated Magical Meal, likely the Blizzard Meal pending the final recipe name. She may regard it as repayment, empowerment, experimentation, or all three. She does not need to conquer the Queen. The Queen eats from Lillia's hand because she remembers the child who cared for her. The meal changes the Queen, then her colony and surrounding ecosystem. Kap's Pond, the aggressive insects, the unnatural eggs, and the frozen north all grow from this betrayal of trust.

callouts.label: Player knowledge
callouts.text: Lillia used a torn recipe page and the Queen's trust to create the Ice Queen; the exact final meal name remains subject to recipe canon.

callouts.label: Story consequence
callouts.text: Every major environmental clue in Act I resolves into one causal chain leading back to Lillia and Tohm's lost pages.

chapters.title: Preparing for the Hive
chapters.subtitle: Every system introduced in Act I becomes part of Gwen's plan.
chapters.era: Act I — The Queen Beneath the Frost
chapters.shortDescription: Every system introduced in Act I becomes part of Gwen's plan.
chapters.overviewText: Gwen prepares to enter the heart of the insect kingdom with everything Act I has taught her. She carries her sword, Fire Meal portions, healing ales, tonics, snacks, charms, gathered ingredients, Oswin's knowledge, Cedric's information, Juno's training, and the incomplete truth Tohm finally shared.

pages.title: Preparing for the Hive
pages.text:
Gwen prepares to enter the heart of the insect kingdom with everything Act I has taught her. She carries her sword, Fire Meal portions, healing ales, tonics, snacks, charms, gathered ingredients, Oswin's knowledge, Cedric's information, Juno's training, and the incomplete truth Tohm finally shared.

The preparation makes the final dungeon feel earned rather than detached from the rest of the act. Gathering supplied the food, cooking created the power, friendships supplied knowledge and training, and each earlier boss taught a survival skill Gwen now needs. The Ice Queen is not waiting at the end of an unrelated cave; the whole act has been teaching Gwen how to reach her.

callouts.label: Player knowledge
callouts.text: Gwen now understands the Queen's origin and deliberately assembles tools from every major Act I system.

callouts.label: Story consequence
callouts.text: The exploration, cooking, combat, and relationship arcs converge into the final dungeon.

chapters.title: Entering the Ice Queen's Hive
chapters.subtitle: The geography of Gwen's first vision becomes the path to the final boss.
chapters.era: Act I — The Queen Beneath the Frost
chapters.shortDescription: The geography of Gwen's first vision becomes the path to the final boss.
chapters.overviewText: The deeper Gwen travels, the more familiar the hive becomes. Frozen roots twist through the same shapes she saw in the trance. Egg chambers, tunnels, and insect silhouettes repeat the memory's visual language.

pages.title: Entering the Ice Queen's Hive
pages.text:
The deeper Gwen travels, the more familiar the hive becomes. Frozen roots twist through the same shapes she saw in the trance. Egg chambers, tunnels, and insect silhouettes repeat the memory's visual language.

This recognition confirms that the Fire Meal did not create an arbitrary symbolic landscape. It connected Gwen to a memory rooted in this exact place and in the relationship between Lillia and the Queen. At the hive's center, cold and insect activity become overwhelming. The ruler who once sustained the forest is waiting inside the disaster created through her trust.

callouts.label: Player knowledge
callouts.text: The trance showed a memory attached to the real hive, and Gwen is now physically retracing it.

callouts.label: Story consequence
callouts.text: The first Magical Meal vision pays off as spatial and emotional preparation for the Queen's chamber.

chapters.title: The Ice Queen
chapters.subtitle: A scar connects the ancient ruler, the child's memory, and the monster before Gwen.
chapters.era: Act I — The Queen Beneath the Frost
chapters.shortDescription: A scar connects the ancient ruler, the child's memory, and the monster before Gwen.
chapters.overviewText: The Ice Queen is enormous and ancient, with the original Ant Queen still visible beneath armor-like magical ice. Her colony fills the surrounding hive and answers her commands. Then Gwen notices a scar: the old wound the child tended in the trance.

pages.title: The Ice Queen
pages.text:
The Ice Queen is enormous and ancient, with the original Ant Queen still visible beneath armor-like magical ice. Her colony fills the surrounding hive and answers her commands. Then Gwen notices a scar: the old wound the child tended in the trance.

The final visual clue resolves what Gwen has learned. The giant shadowed creature was this Queen before corruption. Lillia knew her, cared for her, and later returned with the meal that transformed her. Gwen is not facing a random monster. She is facing a ruler whose capacity to trust was used as the doorway for corruption.

callouts.label: Player knowledge
callouts.text: Gwen directly recognizes the Queen by the wound shown in her trance.

callouts.label: Story consequence
callouts.text: The emotional mystery resolves immediately before combat, changing what victory means.

pages.title: Phase One — The Armored Queen
pages.text:
The first phase emphasizes the Queen's enormous body and control of the hive. She summons insect swarms, raises ice walls and spikes, freezes sections of the arena, launches blizzard zones, and calls smaller creatures from egg chambers. Gwen uses the Fire Meal to burn paths through the swarm, melt barriers, and break the Queen's frozen armor.

The battle tests lessons from the Prawnhusk, Magical Boar, Thairrott, Juno, and the northern caverns. Gwen survives through timing, movement, gathered supplies, and controlled culinary power. When the outer frozen form breaks, the arena falls briefly still. The apparent victory is only the transition.

callouts.label: Player knowledge
callouts.text: Fire counters the Queen's frozen armor, but destroying that armor does not free or defeat her.

callouts.label: Story consequence
callouts.text: The monstrous first form breaks and reveals a second form shaped by corrupted beauty.

pages.title: Phase Two — The Ice Ballerina
pages.text:
The Queen emerges tall, thin, elegant, and disturbing. Her limbs extend into crystalline forms and her movement becomes dance-like. Spins create blade arcs, rings of ice expand with rhythm, frozen trails redraw the arena, and leaps end in precise spike formations. The player must watch, move, wait, and strike as though learning the Queen's dance.

Beneath the storm, Gwen hears the same lullaby from her trance. Some part of the Ant Queen remembers Lillia singing beside her wound. The memory does not cure the corruption, but it makes the tragedy impossible to ignore. Gwen's hesitation nearly kills her. She draws on the last of the Fire Meal, meets frost with flame, and lands the killing strike. The corrupted magic fractures and the Ice Queen dies.

callouts.label: Player knowledge
callouts.text: The Queen retains a fragmented memory of Lillia's childhood kindness even while the corrupted meal controls what she has become.

callouts.label: Story consequence
callouts.text: Gwen ends the magical winter, but the victory is framed as the death of a corrupted ally rather than the destruction of an evil species.

chapters.title: The Recipe Page
chapters.subtitle: The first recovered page shows the complete memory of the Queen's betrayal.
chapters.era: Act I — The Queen Beneath the Frost
chapters.shortDescription: The first recovered page shows the complete memory of the Queen's betrayal.
chapters.overviewText: After the Queen dies, Gwen finds a torn page associated with the ice meal that caused the transformation. The page is most likely the Blizzard Meal recipe, though the final name remains editable until confirmed.

pages.title: The Recipe Page
pages.text:
After the Queen dies, Gwen finds a torn page associated with the ice meal that caused the transformation. The page is most likely the Blizzard Meal recipe, though the final name remains editable until confirmed.

Touching it releases another memory. Gwen sees Lillia clearly, sees the Ant Queen before corruption, and watches Lillia offer the meal. The Queen accepts because she recognizes and trusts her. Then the corruption begins. The page confirms that Lillia did not conquer the Queen by force. She weaponized a relationship built through real kindness, using knowledge torn from Tohm's recipe book.

callouts.label: Player knowledge
callouts.text: The recovered page reveals the complete cause of the Ice Queen transformation and ties it directly to Lillia's stolen recipes.

callouts.label: Story consequence
callouts.text: Gwen recovers the first major recipe page and gains proof that the larger crisis extends beyond Whisker Woods.

chapters.title: The Thaw
chapters.subtitle: Whisker Woods survives, but the damage does not vanish with the Queen.
chapters.era: Act I — The Queen Beneath the Frost
chapters.shortDescription: Whisker Woods survives, but the damage does not vanish with the Queen.
chapters.overviewText: The magical winter begins to end. Ice melts, streams move again, and insects stop behaving like a coordinated hostile army. Some return underground, some scatter, and others seem confused, as though waking from a shared nightmare.

pages.title: The Thaw
pages.text:
The magical winter begins to end. Ice melts, streams move again, and insects stop behaving like a coordinated hostile army. Some return underground, some scatter, and others seem confused, as though waking from a shared nightmare.

The recovery is incomplete. Kap's Pond still needs healing, corrupted areas remain, and some transformed creatures may never return to what they were. Other recipe pages are still loose in the world, Lillia remains beyond Gwen's reach, and Tohm still possesses truths he has not surrendered. Whisker Woods survives the immediate disaster without pretending that one boss fight repairs an ecosystem overnight.

callouts.label: Player knowledge
callouts.text: Defeating the Queen ends the magical coordination and blizzard, but leaves lasting environmental and personal consequences.

callouts.label: Story consequence
callouts.text: The region begins recovering while the recipe-page hunt becomes the larger direction of the game.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.subtitle: The people Gwen met turn a regional victory back into daily life.
chapters.era: Act I — The Queen Beneath the Frost
chapters.shortDescription: The people Gwen met turn a regional victory back into daily life.
chapters.overviewText: Smaller reunions let Whisker Woods breathe after the hive. Brambrake insists that 'his side' survived and avoids admitting the crisis affected everyone. Cedric tries to turn Gwen's victory into a charm promotion and offers an insulting commemorative discount. Juno asks whether fighting a ballerina-shaped insect counts as dance training.

pages.title: Aftermath
pages.text:
Smaller reunions let Whisker Woods breathe after the hive. Brambrake insists that 'his side' survived and avoids admitting the crisis affected everyone. Cedric tries to turn Gwen's victory into a charm promotion and offers an insulting commemorative discount. Juno asks whether fighting a ballerina-shaped insect counts as dance training.

Kap returns to the difficult work of restoring his pond. Gwen's Academy rival requests another Cook Battle when the roads are safer. Oswin remains suspicious of Tohm; if anything, the recovered recipe page proves that his questions were necessary. The humor does not erase the losses, but it restores the community tone that the blizzard threatened.

callouts.label: Player knowledge
callouts.text: The supporting cast survives the crisis with relationships changed but unresolved.

callouts.label: Story consequence
callouts.text: Act I closes its local character loops while keeping Tohm's secrecy and the wider corruption alive.

chapters.title: Gwen and Tohm

pages.title: Gwen and Tohm
pages.text:
Back at the tavern, Gwen places the recovered recipe page in front of Tohm. She now knows enough to recognize the shape of his silence: he knew Lillia, understood Magical Meals, possessed the recipe book from which the pages were torn, and knew those pages could transform living creatures.

Tohm does not give her the entire truth. He is still hiding his deeper involvement with the Dragon Knife, Lillia's first dark meal, Tabby Island, and the Cat Cauldron. Gwen tells him that one day he will tell her everything. Tohm knows she is right. They look toward the recovering forest with the immediate crisis ended and their real journey beginning. Act I leaves Gwen stronger, officially a chef, and no longer willing to accept mystery as an answer from the mentor she loves.

callouts.label: Player knowledge
callouts.text: Gwen knows Tohm is connected to Lillia and the pages, but neither Gwen nor the player receives every late-game secret yet.

callouts.label: Story consequence
callouts.text: The Act I conflict resolves into the long-term recipe-page recovery quest and a growing demand for truth from Tohm.

chapters.title: The Truth of Tabby Island
chapters.subtitle: The hidden wound in Tohm's past waits beneath the story.
chapters.era: Late Game Reveal
chapters.shortDescription: The truth of Tabby Island and the Cat Cauldron reframes Tohm Kyatt, the Whisken exodus, and the Mas'eel hunt for magical recipes.

pages.title: The First Search for What Is Untasted
pages.text: Long before Gwen's journey, ancient Whisken seekers created the Cat Cauldron while trying to improve food and reach the knowledge of what is untasted. The goal began as culinary wonder, but the invention was too powerful for the island beneath it.
pages.imagePlaceholder: Ancient Whisken cooks around an unfinished cauldron under island roots.
pages.caption: The first mistake was born from hunger for knowledge.

pages.title: The First Exodus
pages.text: The Cat Cauldron caused Tabby Island to begin decaying. The ancient Whisken fled, then locked the cauldron at the bottom of the island, removed it from their history books, and stopped speaking of it until the truth was forgotten.
pages.imagePlaceholder: Boats leaving a dim island while elders seal a hidden chamber.
pages.caption: A people can bury a thing so well that their children inherit only the wound.

pages.title: Tohm Finds the Forgotten Cauldron
pages.text: Centuries later, Tohm Kyatt discovers the hidden knowledge and returns to Tabby Island. He cooks a meal in the Cat Cauldron and activates it. A pulse runs into the earth, and the island begins decaying again.
pages.imagePlaceholder: Tohm standing before a cat-shaped cauldron as light cracks through the floor.
pages.caption: The second disaster began with a meal no one else knew he had cooked.

pages.title: The Pulse the Mas'eel Heard
pages.text: The awakened cauldron's pulse does more than damage the island. It lets the Mas'eel Cult sense the power and know it was on Tabby Island. Tohm takes the cauldron and flees in the Living Tavern before anyone understands what happened.
pages.imagePlaceholder: A magical pulse spreading from island roots toward distant black sails.
pages.caption: The island heard decay. The cult heard invitation.

pages.title: False Traders
pages.text: Mas'eel cultists arrive pretending to be traders. They introduce new foods, gain trust over years, secretly sear the island, rise in village influence, and begin persecuting Whisken people for holding to the Triadic faith taught by the Tablemaker.
pages.imagePlaceholder: Friendly trade stalls with beautiful spices casting wrong shadows.
pages.caption: They did not conquer the village first. They fed it lies.

pages.title: The Second Exodus
pages.text: The Whisken flee again, though to them it feels like the first time. Tohm hears what is happening and gets Lel Kai, who is becoming general of the faery army, to send boats. Corruption scatters many of them, and the known survivors eventually reach Whisker Woods.
pages.imagePlaceholder: Rescue boats breaking through corrupted waters toward a forest shore.
pages.caption: The village that remains is a rescued fragment, not the whole story.

chapters.title: The Mas'eel Hunt
chapters.subtitle: A gentle mask hides a cult searching for the cauldron and recipes.
chapters.era: Late Game Reveal
chapters.shortDescription: The Mas'eel corrupt the shared Tablemaker faith into FEAST, hunt the Cat Cauldron, and tie Tabby Island's past to Princess Lillia's present danger.

pages.title: FEAST Instead of Three Pillars
pages.text: Most cultures worship the Tablemaker and practice the Triadic faith through their own traditions. The Mas'eel compress Passion, Taste, and Love into FEAST, turning shared abundance into control, hunger, and power.
pages.imagePlaceholder: Three warm dots reflected in a single distorted black eye.
pages.caption: A holy meal becomes dangerous when love is removed from the recipe.

pages.title: Mur'amar's Gentle Voice
pages.text: Mur'amar can move among villagers as if he belongs, speaking of the Mas'eel faith as something gentle. His danger is not that he looks monstrous. It is that he knows how to sound comforting while asking about the Cat Cauldron, Tohm, and magical recipes.
pages.imagePlaceholder: A peaceful stranger at a village table with a hidden symbol on his sleeve.
pages.caption: Some villains enter through the front door and compliment the soup.

pages.title: Lillia's Alliance
pages.text: After Tabby Island, the Mas'eel search for the Cat Cauldron and Tohm's magical recipes while working with Princess Lillia. Lillia wants power and magical transformation; the Mas'eel want the sacred machinery beneath that power.
pages.imagePlaceholder: A faery-realm camp kitchen where royal banners meet cult marks.
pages.caption: Different hungers can still share a kitchen.

pages.title: What Gwen Must Uncover
pages.text: Gwen's journey eventually becomes more than recovering recipe pages. She must understand which foods heal, which foods corrupt, which histories were erased, and why Tohm's secret brought the Mas'eel into the story.
pages.imagePlaceholder: Gwen arranging recipe pages, spice samples, and island-map clues on a tavern table.
pages.caption: A cookbook can become a case file.

chapters.title: Final Confrontation
chapters.subtitle: Cooking, truth, corruption, and courage reach the same table.
chapters.era: Final Act
chapters.shortDescription: The final confrontation will bring Gwen, Tohm, Lillia, the Recipe Book, Dark Culinary Arts, and the meaning of Food Essence into one decisive story meal.

pages.title: The Last Table
pages.text: The final act should not only defeat a villain. It should answer the story's central question: what is food for? Power, control, survival, memory, love, or the courage to share a table after harm?
pages.imagePlaceholder: A final table between light and corruption.
pages.caption: The end should taste like the whole journey.
